curriculum_chunks.content:
Every day, by the time most teenagers in Egypt have had breakfast, they have already made more **brand choices**(1) than they realize. The phone that wakes them up is one of the most **recognized**(2) **devices**(3) in the world. The shoes by the door carry a **tick**(4) that is far more famous than the company's actual name. Furthermore, the cereal box on the table **features**(5) a **cartoon**(6) bird that has remained unchanged longer than many brands have survived. None of this is an **accident**(7). The biggest companies **invest**(8) more **heavily**(9) in **brand-building**(10) than in almost anything else. This is because a **well-known**(11) brand is more **valuable**(12) than any single product. In addition, they spend more on emotional **storytelling**(13) than on simply describing what their products do.

A brand is much more than a logo. It is a set of feelings and ideas, and the strongest brands build those feelings more carefully and more consistently than smaller companies ever could. When brand X puts its tick on a shoe and writes "Just Do It", it is selling not only shoes, but also the idea that the person who wears them is stronger, more **determined**(14), and more ready for a challenge than someone who does not. Similarly, when a phone brand presents a new phone in a clean white room, it is selling the idea that its products are simpler, more **elegant**(15), and more **desirable**(16) than anything else on the **market**(17).

A **branded**$^{(18)}$ product is almost always more **expensive**$^{(19)}$ than a similar **unbranded**$^{(20)}$ one. Even though the quality difference is often smaller than people expect, they still choose the brand because the feeling it gives them feels **worth**$^{(21)}$ far more than the price difference.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.content:
Psychologists who study how people make choices have found something interesting. When people see the **logo**$^{(22)}$ of their favorite brand, the part of the brain linked to personal **identity**$^{(23)}$ becomes more **active**$^{(24)}$ than when they see an unknown **label**$^{(25)}$. As a result, choosing a brand is rarely a simple or purely **practical**$^{(26)}$ decision. This means that when someone chooses X over Z, they are often making a **deeper choice**$^{(27)}$ than simply picking a more comfortable shoe — they are saying something about who they are, or who they most want to be. Understanding why we prefer one brand to another can be an important step towards **mindful consumption**$^{(28)}$. For instance, for many young people in Egypt, wearing the most popular brand feels more important than wearing the most practical one, because brands have become one of the most powerful languages we use to show where we **belong**$^{(29)}$. Admittedly, not everyone is equally influenced by brand image.

Although companies benefit greatly from this power, the influence of brands also raises one of the most important questions in modern life: are we truly free when we make choices, or do companies create our **preference**$^{(30)}$ for us? On the other hand, understanding how brands work gives us a real **advantage**$^{(31)}$ as consumers. This helps us avoid blind brand loyalty, where we buy a product based on emotion rather than quality. The most successful brands do not just sell products. They sell the feeling of **belonging**$^{(32)}$ somewhere. Consequently, this feeling becomes stronger, and far more personal. It also becomes harder to **resist**$^{(33)}$ than any simple **advertisement**$^{(34)}$ could ever be. Overall, the more **aware**$^{(35)}$ we are of how brands shape our thinking, the better and freer our choices can become.

curriculum_chunks.content:
مقال الرأي

**1. What is an opinion article?**
ما هو مقال الرأي؟
An opinion article is a piece of writing in which the writer gives a clear opinion about a topic and supports it with reasons, examples, or evidence.
مقال الرأي هو نوع من الكتابة يعرض فيه الكاتب رأيه بوضوح حول موضوع ما ويدعمه بأسباب أو أمثلة أو أدلة.

**2. What is an opinion article used for?**
فيما يُستخدم مقال الرأي؟
An opinion article is used to persuade readers, explain a viewpoint, and discuss a topic clearly.
يُستخدم مقال الرأي لإقناع القراء وشرح وجهة نظر ومناقشة موضوع بوضوح.

When you write an opinion article, turn your insight into an intervention: don't just observe the world, but use your analysis to pinpoint a specific problem and then provide a clear, actionable path forward. Diagnose the issue, then prescribe the cure.
عندما تكتب مقال الرأي، حوّل رؤيتك إلى تدخّل عملي؛ فلا تكتف بملاحظة ما يحدث في العالم، بل استخدم تحليلك لتحديد مشكلة معينة بدقة، ثم قدّم مسارًا واضحًا وقابلًا للتنفيذ للمضي قدمًا. شخّص المشكلة، ثم اقترح العلاج المناسب.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Opinion Article

curriculum_chunks.content:
الأجزاء الرئيسية لمقال الرأي | Part | Explanation | | :--- | :--- | | **1. Headline**
العنوان | **What is it?**
A headline is a short, clear, and catchy title that introduces the topic and may suggest the writer's opinion.
عنوان قصير وواضح وجذاب يقدّم الموضوع، وقد يلمّح إلى رأي الكاتب.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To attract the reader's attention and prepare them for the main idea of the article.
جذب انتباه القارئ وتهيئته للفكرة الرئيسية في المقال.

**Useful Expressions / Title Patterns:**
- Why We Should Care about...
- The Importance of...
- The Problem with...

- Should We ...?
- The Truth about...
- A Better Way to Think about ...

**e.g.**
Why We Should Care about Healthy Habits |
curriculum_chunks.heading: Main Parts of an opinion article

curriculum_chunks.content:
المقدمة

**What is it?**
The introduction presents the topic and states the writer's main opinion clearly. It should be direct, not too detailed.

المحتوى:
تعرض المقدمة الموضوع وتوضح رأي الكاتب الرئيسي بوضوح. وينبغي أن تكون مباشرة وغير مليئة بالتفاصيل.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To tell the reader what the article is about and what opinion the writer will defend.

إخبار القارئ بموضوع المقال والرأي الذي سيدافع عنه الكاتب.

**Useful Expressions:**
- Nowadays, many people discuss the issue of...
- These days, ... has become an important topic.
- In recent years, people have become interested in ...
- Many people believe that ...
- In my opinion, ... - I believe that ...
- I strongly think that ... - This article will explain why ...

**e.g.**
Nowadays, many people discuss the importance of healthy habits. In my opinion, small daily habits can greatly improve people's lives.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Introduction

curriculum_chunks.content:
**What is it?**
The first body paragraph gives the first strong reason that supports the writer's opinion. It should include an explanation, example, or evidence.

تعرض الفقرة الأساسية الأولى السبب الأول القوي الذي يدعم رأي الكاتب. ويجب أن تتضمن شرحًا أو مثالًا أو دليلًا.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To begin proving the writer's opinion in a clear and logical way.

بدء إثبات رأي الكاتب بطريقة واضحة ومنطقية.

**Useful Expressions:**
- First of all, ... - One important reason is that ...
- The first reason is that ... - To begin with, ...
- This is because ... - For example, ...
- For instance, ... - This shows that ...
- As a result, ...

**e.g.**
First of all, healthy habits can improve people's physical energy. For example, regular exercise helps the body become stronger and more active.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 193 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Body Paragraph 1

curriculum_chunks.content:
**What is it?**
The second body paragraph gives another reason that supports the writer’s opinion. It should add a new idea, not repeat the first reason.
تعرض الفقرة الأساسية الثانية سببًا آخر يدعم رأي الكاتب. ويجب أن تضيف فكرة جديدة، لا أن تكرر السبب الأول.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To develop the argument and make the opinion stronger and more convincing.
تطوير الحجة وجعل الرأي أقوى وأكثر إقناعًا.

**Useful Expressions:**
- Another reason is that ...
- Moreover, ...
- Furthermore, ...
- A clear example of this is ...
- In addition, ...
- What is more, ...
- This can also help ...
- This can lead to ...

**e.g.**
In addition, healthy habits can improve mental well-being. People who sleep well and eat balanced meals often feel calmer and more focused.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4. Body Paragraph 2

curriculum_chunks.content:
عرض الرأي الآخر والرد عليه

**What is it?**
The concession presents one reasonable point from the opposite view. Then the writer responds to it and shows why their own opinion is still stronger.
تعرض فقرة التنازل نقطة منطقية من الرأي الآخر، ثم يرد الكاتب عليها ويوضح لماذا يظل رأيه أقوى.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To show fairness, balance, and maturity in thinking.
إظهار الإنصاف والتوازن والنضج في التفكير.

**Useful Expressions:**
- Some people may argue that ...
- Others believe that ...
- Some people think that ...
- Although this may be true, ...
- However, ...
- On the other hand, ...
- This point is understandable, but ...
- It is true that ...
- Nevertheless, ...

**e.g.**
Some people may argue that changing daily habits is difficult. However, even small changes can make a clear difference over time.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 194 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5. Concession

curriculum_chunks.content:
الخاتمة

**What is it?**
The conclusion restates the writer's opinion in different words and ends with a strong final message. It should not introduce a new reason.

تعيد الخاتمة صياغة رأي الكاتب بكلمات مختلفة وتنتهي برسالة أخيرة قوية. ولا ينبغي أن تضيف سببًا جديدًا.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To close the article clearly and leave the reader with a final idea.

إنهاء المقال بوضوح وترك فكرة أخيرة لدى القارئ.

**Useful Expressions:**
- In conclusion, ...
- All in all, ...
- It is clear that ...
- Overall, I believe that ...
- We should remember that ...
- To sum up, ...
- For these reasons, ...
- Therefore, we should ...

**e.g.**
In conclusion, I believe that healthy habits are essential for a better life. We should remember that small changes can lead to great results.

curriculum_chunks.content: Many teenagers use **social media**(1) every day without thinking about how these **apps**(2) really work. Although these **platforms**(3) seem free, they actually **collect information**(4) about users' **behavior**(5) and **interests**(6). Apps are carefully **designed**(7) to keep people online longer through **features**(8) that make it hard to stop **scrolling**(9). While social media has **benefits**(10), it is important for users to understand how their time and **attention**(11) are being used.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Digital Consumption

curriculum_chunks.content:
**1. You have probably heard this phrase before:**

'If you are not paying for the **product**(12), you are the product.' Most people use social media apps for free. But nothing is ever truly free. Every minute you spend scrolling, the app is collecting **data**(13) about you — what you like, what you **ignore**(14), how long you stop on each image, and what makes you **react**(15). This data is then sold to companies who want to show you **advertisements**(16). Your time and attention are not free; they are being bought and sold.

**2. Apps are designed to keep you online for as long as possible.**

Features like **infinite scroll**(17) where the **feed**(18) never ends, and **autoplay**(19), where the next video starts automatically were not created by accident. They were built by teams of **designers**(20) and **professionals**(21) whose job was to make you stay on the app. By the age of 17, the **average**(22) teenager has already spent more time on social media than in all their years of school.

curriculum_chunks.content: Research has found that simply receiving a **notification**$^{(23)}$ — even if you do not open it — can make it harder to focus on a task. Your **brain**$^{(24)}$ is waiting for the **reward**$^{(25)}$ of checking the message, and this waiting **takes up**$^{(26)}$ **mental energy**$^{(27)}$. Students who keep their phones **nearby**$^{(28)}$ while studying perform less well than those who put their phones in another room.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. The effects on concentration are also serious.

curriculum_chunks.content:
None of this means that apps and social media are completely bad. They help people stay **connected**$^{(29)}$, access **information**$^{(30)}$, and be **creative**$^{(31)}$. However, it is important to understand how these platforms work, and who **benefits from**$^{(32)}$ your time online. The first step to being in control of your **digital habits**$^{(33)}$ is simply knowing that your attention has a **value**$^{(34)}$. Companies have always known this. Now it is time for users to know it too.

curriculum_chunks.content:
**A review:** is a critical evaluation of a subject such as a book, product, service, performance, or piece of writing. Its primary purpose is to provide an informed opinion that helps others decide whether they should engage with that subject or avoid it.

المراجعة النقدية: هي تقييم نقدي لموضوع ما، مثل كتاب أو منتج أو خدمة أو عرض أو عمل كتابي، ويتمثل هدفها الأساسي في تقديم رأي قائم على المعرفة يساعد الآخرين على تحديد ما إذا كان ينبغي لهم تجربة ذلك الموضوع أو التعامل معه أم تجنبه.

**What is a review used for?**

A review is used to help readers decide whether something is useful, enjoyable, effective, or suitable for them. It gives information, examples, and personal judgement in a balanced and professional way.

فيما تُستخدم المراجعة النقدية؟
تُستخدم المراجعة / العرض التقييمي لمساعدة القراء على تحديد ما إذا كان الشيء مفيدًا أو ممتعًا أو فعالًا أو مناسبًا لهم. وهي تقدم معلومات وأمثلة وحكمًا شخصيًا بطريقة متوازنة ومهنية.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Review

curriculum_chunks.content:
الأجزاء الرئيسية للمراجعة النقدية | Part | Explanation | | :--- | :--- | | **1. Introduction**
المقدمة | The introduction names the subject of the review and gives essential background information. It also states the writer's overall impression in one sentence.

تذكر المقدمة موضوع المراجعة، وتقدم معلومات أساسية عنه، وتوضح الانطباع العام للكاتب في جملة واحدة.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To introduce what is being reviewed and prepare the reader for the writer's judgement.

تقديم الشيء الذي تم مراجعته وتهيئة القارئ لرأي الكاتب.

**Useful Expressions:**
- ... is a [type] designed for.
- This review looks at ...
- At first glance, ... appears to ...
- Overall, it seems to be ...

**e.g.**
At first glance, this learning app appears to be simple, useful, and suitable for teenagers. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: Main Parts of a review

curriculum_chunks.content:
This paragraph describes the strengths of the subject. It should include specific examples or evidence and explain why each point is positive.

تعرض هذه الفقرة نقاط القوة في الشيء الذي تتم مراجعته، مع أمثلة أو أدلة محددة، وتوضح سبب اعتبار كل نقطة إيجابية.

**Purpose:** الغرض

To show what is good, useful, impressive, or effective about the subject.

توضيح الجوانب الجيدة أو المفيدة أو المميزة في الشيء الذي تتم مراجعته.

**Useful Expressions:**

- One of its greatest strengths is ...
- What makes it particularly impressive is ...
- Research has shown that ...
- A useful feature is ...
- It helps users to ...

**e.g.**

One of its greatest strengths is that it helps users access information quickly and stay organized.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Positives الإيجابيات

curriculum_chunks.content:
This paragraph discusses the weaknesses or limitations fairly. The writer should avoid being too harsh and should use a balanced, professional tone.

تناقش هذه الفقرة بنصاف نقاط الضعف أو النواقص. ويجب أن يتجنب الكاتب القسوة الزائدة وأن يستخدم أسلوبًا متوازنًا ومهنيًا.

**Purpose:** الغرض

To show balance by explaining what could be improved or what may cause problems.

إظهار التوازن من خلال توضيح ما يمكن تحسينه أو ما قد يسبب مشكلات.

**Useful Expressions:**

- It is worth noting that ...
- However, it is not without its flaws.
- On the other hand, ...
- A significant drawback is that ...
- One limitation is ...

**e.g.**

However, it is not without its flaws. Too many notifications can affect users' concentration.

curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Negatives السلبيات

curriculum_chunks.content:
الخاتمة

The conclusion summarises the writer's overall judgement. It states who the writer would recommend the subject to and why. It should end with a memorable final sentence.

تلخص الخاتمة الحكم العام للكاتب، وتوضح لمن يوصي بهذا الشيء ولماذا، وينبغي أن تنتهي بجملة أخيرة مؤثرة.

**Purpose:** الغرض
To give the final judgement and make a clear recommendation.
تقديم الحكم النهائي وإعطاء توصية واضحة.

**Useful Expressions:**
- Overall, I would recommend ... to ...
- In conclusion, ... is suitable for ...
- For these reasons, ...
- I would not recommend it for ...
- It is a good choice for ...

**e.g.**
Overall, I would recommend this app to students who want a simple way to organize their study time.

curriculum_chunks.heading: The Psychology of the Sale

curriculum_chunks.content:
Every year, millions of people around the world wait for events like Black Friday to go shopping. They feel excited as they plan their purchases(8) in advance(9) and they believe they are making smart choices(10). But are they really saving money, or are they falling for(11) a set of very clever tricks?

One of the most common tricks is called loss aversion(12). Imagine a jacket that costs 400 Egyptian pounds. You do not really need it. Then a sign appears: "Was 800 LE, Now 400 LE, Save 50%!" Suddenly, the jacket feels much more attractive(13). Your brain(14) tells you, 'If I don't buy it, I will lose the chance(15) to save 400 pounds.' Of course, you have not lost anything, but that is how our brains work. Not buying something feels like a loss.

Sale events also use other tricks. Phrases like 'Only 3 left in stock(16)!' create a feeling of urgency. You feel that you must decide immediately or you will miss the chance. When you see many other people buying something, you think it must be a good idea. And countdown(17) clocks on websites force you to decide quickly, before you have time to think carefully. All three tricks work together to push you towards buying.

Research has found something surprising: people who shop during sales actually spend more money overall(18) than people who do not. They feel they have saved money, but in fact they have spent more. The sale is not designed(19) to save you money. It is designed to make you spend more and feel happy about it.

curriculum_chunks.content:

- as

\+ subject + verb (full clause)

curriculum_chunks.heading: Rule:

<!-- بداية الصفحة 236 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Note that:

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Rule:**
$\rightarrow$ Cause sentence. As a result / As a consequence, + effect sentence.

**e.g.**
* Ice sheets are melting. **As a result**, sea levels are rising.
* Fossil fuels release carbon dioxide. **As a consequence**, heat is trapped in the atmosphere.

**Position:** at the beginning of a new sentence, followed by a comma.
تأتي هذه التعبيرات في بداية جملة جديدة ويليها فاصلة:
**e.g.** Ice is melting fast. **As a result**, sea levels are rising.
في اللغة الدارجة، يمكن أن تأتي هذه التعبيرات في نهاية الجملة:
**e.g.** Ice is melting fast. Sea levels are rising **as a result**.

**Note that:**
$\rightarrow$ Effect sentence + as a result of / as a consequence of + noun/gerund.

**e.g.**
* Crops failed **as a result of extreme heat**.
* Sea levels are rising **as a consequence of melting ice**.

تُستخدم هذه التعبيرات بمعنى (كنتيجة لـ)، وفي هذه الحالة يأتي بعدها اسم أو فعل مضاف له (ing) ويمكن أن تأتي في البداية أو الوسط.
**e.g.** **As a result of the ice melting fast**, sea levels are rising.
= Sea levels are rising **as a result of the ice melting fast**.

**Common mistake خطأ شائع**
يجب وضع فاصلة بعد (as a result/as a consequence) عندما تأتي في بداية الجملة الثانية:
$\times$ Ice is melting fast. **As a result** sea levels are rising.
$\checkmark$ Ice is melting fast. **As a result**, sea levels are rising.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3 As a result / as a consequence + new sentence نتيجة لذلك

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Rule:**
$\rightarrow$ Cause sentence. Therefore / Consequently, + effect sentence.

**e.g.**
* Temperatures are rising. **Therefore**, action is urgent.
* Floods destroy harvests. **Consequently**, food security is threatened.

**Position:** at the beginning of a new sentence, followed by a comma.
تأتي في بداية جملة جديدة ويليها فاصلة:
**e.g.** It rained heavily. **Therefore, the match was cancelled**.
= The match was cancelled **because it rained heavily**.

**Common mistake خطأ شائع**
يجب وضع فاصلة بعد (Therefore/Consequently) عندما تأتي في بداية الجملة الثانية.
$\times$ Ice is melting fast. **Therefore** sea levels are rising.
$\checkmark$ Ice is melting fast. **Therefore**, sea levels are rising.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 237 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 Therefore, / Consequently, + new sentence لذلك / ومن ثم

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم (**That's why**) بمعنى (لهذا السبب) في بداية الجملة الثانية ولا يأتي بعدها فاصلة.

$$\rightarrow \text{cause sentence.} + \text{That's why} + \text{effect sentence}$$

**e.g.** $\rightarrow$ • Ice melts. That's why sea levels are rising.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Note that:

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Rule:**
$$\rightarrow \text{Cause sentence, so + effect sentence.}$$

**e.g.** $\rightarrow$ 
• Temperatures are rising, **so** ice is melting faster.
• Rainfall patterns are changing, **so** crop production is falling.

**Position:** in the middle of the sentence, right after a comma.
تأتي (**so**) في وسط الجملة مباشرة بعد الفاصلة:
**e.g.** Ice is melting fast, **so** sea levels are rising.

تأتي (**so**) أحياناً في بداية جملة جديدة بمعنى (لذلك / لذا).
في اللغة الحديثة، يمكن أن تبدأ (**so**) جملة لتقديم النتيجة، ولكنها أقل رسمية من:
- therefore / consequently / as a result
**e.g.** The ice is melting fast. **So**, sea levels are rising.

**Note that:**
$$\rightarrow \text{... so + result نتيجة} \neq \text{... so that + purpose غرض}$$

**e.g.** $\rightarrow$ 
• Ice is melting fast, **so** sea levels are rising. (result)
• We must act now **so that** future generations can inherit a safe planet. (purpose)

تُستخدم الفاصلة دائماً قبل (**so**) عند ربط جملتين تامين؛ وهذا يختلف عن (**because**) التي لا تحتاج إلى فاصلة قبلها عندما تأتي في المنتصف.
**e.g.** Ice is melting fast, **so** sea levels are rising.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 So + effect clause لذلك

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Rule:**

• lead (s) to
• result (s) in
• cause (s)
\+ noun phrase / gerund phrase

**e.g.** $\rightarrow$ 
• Rising temperature **leads to** melting ice.
• Ocean warming **results in** coral bleaching.
• Extreme heat **causes** crop failure.

**Position:** in the middle of the sentence, as the main verb.
تأتي هذه الأفعال ضمن بناء الجملة كفعل رئيسي:
**e.g.** Poor sleep **leads to** tiredness.
= Poor sleep **causes** tiredness.

**Common mistake:**
خطأ شائع:
نستخدم بعد (**lead to, result in**) اسماً أو فعلاً بإضافة (**ing**)، وليس جملة كاملة.
 Rising temperatures lead to **ice melts**.
 Rising temperatures lead to **melting ice**.

curriculum_chunks.heading: 6 Lead (s) to / result(s) in / cause(s) + noun / gerund يؤدي إلى

curriculum_chunks.content: Our planet's climate is changing faster than at any point in recorded history. In this lesson, you will explore the science behind the climate crisis, examine its wide-ranging effects on people and ecosystems, and consider what urgent action looks like.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Climate Crisis

curriculum_chunks.content: The Earth's **climate**(1) is changing at a never-before-seen **rate**(2). Scientists around the world agree that human activity is the primary **driver**(3) of what we now call the **climate crisis**(4). Since the Industrial Revolution, the burning of **fossil fuels**(5) – coal, oil, and natural gas – has released billions of tons of **carbon dioxide**(6) (CO₂) into the **atmosphere**(7). As a consequence, these emissions create what is known as the **Greenhouse Effect**(8), which traps heat and raises global temperatures.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text

curriculum_chunks.content: The effects are already being felt across the planet. In the Arctic, ice sheets are melting at an **alarming rate**(9). **Glaciers**(10) that have existed for thousands of years are getting smaller. As a result of this rapid melting, **sea levels**(11) are rising, threatening coastal communities and low-lying island nations. Scientists predict that without immediate action, sea levels could rise by up to one meter by 2100, making hundreds of millions of people homeless.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Melting ice & rising seas

curriculum_chunks.content: Extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and more severe. Because of rising global temperatures, **hurricanes**(12), wildfires, droughts, and floods are occurring with greater **intensity**(13). In 2023 alone, wildfires damaged parts of Canada, Greece, and Australia. Record-breaking temperatures were recorded on every continent. Consequently, the human and economic cost of these disasters is shocking and continues to grow each year.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Extreme weather events

curriculum_chunks.content: **Biodiversity**(14) is also under serious threat. Since habitats shift and temperatures change, countless **species**(15) struggle to adapt. Coral reefs, often called the rainforests of the sea, are dying due to ocean warming and **acidification**(16). As a result, the Great Barrier Reef has experienced mass **bleaching**(17) events repeatedly in recent years. Experts warn that human activity has led to the sixth mass extinction event in Earth's history.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Biodiversity loss

curriculum_chunks.content: Agriculture and food security are at risk too. Due to changing rainfall patterns and extreme heat, **crop**$^{(18)}$ production is being reduced in many parts of the world. curriculum_chunks.content:
An argumentative paragraph is a structured unit of writing that focuses on a single, debatable claim supported by evidence, reasoning, and analysis. Its primary purpose is to persuade the reader to accept a specific viewpoint or take a particular action.

الفقرة الجدلية هي وحدة كتابية منظمة تركز على ادعاء (رأي) واحد قابل للنقاش، وتدعمه بالأدلة والاستدلال والتحليل. ويتمثل هدفها الأساسي في إقناع القارئ بقبول وجهة نظر محددة أو اتخاذ إجراء معين.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Argumentative Paragraph الفقرة الجدلية

curriculum_chunks.content:
State your opinion clearly. This is the main idea of the paragraph.
اذكر رأيك بوضوح. هذه هي الفكرة الرئيسية للفقرة.

**Purpose الغرض**
To state your opinion clearly; show the reader the main idea of the paragraph from the start.
لتوضيح رأيك بشكل واضح، قم بتقديم الفكرة الرئيسية للفقرة للقارئ منذ البداية.

**Useful Expressions:**
- It is clear that ...
- I strongly believe ...
- There is no doubt that ...

**e.g.** I strongly believe that human activity is the main cause of climate change.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. Topic Sentence جملة الفكرة الرئيسية

curriculum_chunks.content:
Give 2 - 3 reasons or pieces of evidence to support your opinion.
قدم سببين أو ثلاثة أسباب أو أدلة لدعم رأيك.

**Purpose الغرض**
To support your opinion with reasons and evidence, and to show the result each reason produces.
لدعم رأيك بالأسباب والأدلة، وتوضيح النتيجة التي يؤدي إليها كل سبب.

**Useful Expressions:**
- First, ...
- Furthermore, ...
- In addition, ...
- As a result, ...
- Because of this, ...
- Therefore, ...

**e.g.** This is because burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. As a result, more heat is trapped and global temperatures rise.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 241 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Supporting Sentences الجُمل الداعمة

curriculum_chunks.content:
ذكر الرأي المخالف

Mention the opposite view, then refute it. This makes your argument stronger.
اذكر الرأي المخالف ثم ردّ عليه. وهذا يجعل فقرتك أقوى.

**Purpose** الغرض
To show balance by acknowledging the opposite view fairly before responding to it.
لإظهار التوازن من خلال الاعتراف بالرأي المخالف بإنصاف قبل الرد عليه.

**Useful Expressions:**
- Although some people believe ...
- While it is true that ...
- However, ...

**e.g.** Some people argue that climate change is natural. However, the current speed of change is strongly linked to human activity.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Concession

curriculum_chunks.content:
الخاتمة

Restate your opinion in different words. Do not introduce a new idea.
أعد صياغة رأيك بكلمات مختلفة، ولا تقدم فكرة جديدة.

**Purpose** الغرض
To restate your opinion strongly and end the paragraph without adding a new idea.
لإعادة صياغة رأيك بقوة وإنهاء الفقرة دون إضافة فكرة جديدة.

**Useful Expressions:**
- In conclusion, ...
- Therefore, it is evident that ...
- To sum up, ...

**e.g.** Therefore, reducing human emissions is essential for protecting the planet.

curriculum_chunks.heading: Complete the sentences using the correct form of the word in brackets.

curriculum_chunks.content:
١ تُستخدم (should/ought to + inf) لإعطاء النصيحة المُثبتة:
- You should take a break between work hours.
= I advise you to take a break between work hours.
= It is advisable that you take a break between work hours.

٢ تُستخدم (shouldn't/oughtn't to + inf) لإعطاء النصيحة المنفية:
- You should not eat much rice. (OR: shouldn't eat)
= I advise you not to eat much rice.
= It is inadvisable that you eat much rice.

٣ لاحظ ما يلي:
→ ... should / shouldn't + inf. ...
- You should do a sport to keep fit.
- You shouldn't eat junk food.

→ = ... ought to / ought not to + inf. ...
- You ought to do a sport to keep fit.
- You ought not (oughtn't) to eat junk food.

→ = ... had better / had better not + inf. ...
- You'd better do a sport to keep fit.
- You'd better not eat junk food.

تذكر أن:
١. الاختصار ('d) في (had better) هو اختصار لـ (had) وليس (would):
- You'd better take a rest. = You had better take a rest. (NOT: would better)

٢. نفي (had better) هو (had better not) وليس (hadn't better):
- You'd better not waste your time. (NOT: hadn't better)

curriculum_chunks.content:

→ ... should/ought to + have + p.p. ...
- I should have saved my money. = I ought to have saved my money.
= I could have saved my money.

- هناك حالات كثيرة لإستخدام (may/might + inf.) منها:

**1 Possibility: present and future**
التعبير عن احتمالية/إمكانية حدوث شيء في المضارع أو المستقبل:
... may/might + inf. ...
- We might meet at Omar's wedding party.
= We will possibly meet at Omar's wedding party.
= It is possible that we will meet at Omar's wedding party.
- Sama may help mum with the housework.
= Sama will probably help mum with the housework.
= It is probable that Sama will help mum with the housework.

**Remember:**
What is the difference between 'may' and 'might'?
ما الفرق بين كل من 'may' و 'might' في التعبير عن الإمكانية في المضارع أو المُستقبل؟
- بالرغم من التشابه الكبير بينهما في هذا الإستخدام، فإن (may) تُستخدم للتعبير عن حدث مُرجَّح حُدوثه، بينما تُستخدم (might) مع خُذف إمكانية حدوثه ضعيفة:
- I may go shopping. = I probably will go shopping.
= It is more likely that I will go shopping.
- I might go shopping. = It is unlikely that I will go shopping.

**2 may/might/could + have + p.p.**
Possibility: past
تُستخدم الصيغة التالية في التعبير عن احتمالية/إمكانية أن شيء ما قد حدث في الماضي (استنتاج يقوم على دليل ضعيف):

**2) تستخدم (mustn't + inf.) للتعبير عن المنع أو التحريم أو عدم السماح قانوناً بعمل شيء:**
- You mustn't park here. It is not allowed.
- You mustn't touch the objects in the museum.

**3) تستخدم (mustn't + inf.) لإعطاء النصيحة القوية (لشخص مقرّب):**
- You mustn't smoke!

**4) تستخدم (mustn't + inf.) للتعبير عن أنه من المهم عدم القيام بشيء معين:**
- I mustn't leave my keys inside the office again.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 must not (mustn't) + inf. يجب ألا / ممنوع أن / غير مسموح بـ

curriculum_chunks.content:
**1) لاحظ الصيغ المختلفة لـ (have / has + to + inf.):**

$\rightarrow$ **He / She / It + has to + inf. ....**
- Sama **has to pay** the bills الفواتير on time. (إثبات)
- Ahmed **doesn't have to get up** early at weekends. (Not: hasn't to) (نفي)
- **Does** Rodayna **have to study** history at school? (Not: Has Rodayna ...) (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- When **does** Leen **have to finish** the report? (Not: When has ...) (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

$\rightarrow$ **I / We / You / They + have to + inf. ....**
- I **have to pass** the driving test to get a licence. (إثبات)
- They **don't have to leave** now. (Not: haven't to) (نفي)
- **Do** we **have to arrive** at school before seven? (Not: Have we ...) (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- Why **do** you **have to work** so long hours? (Not: Why have...) (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

**2) تستخدم (have / has + to + inf.) للتعبير عن الإلزام الخارجي (ليس للفاعل اختيار آخر) ويشمل ذلك الإلزام الذي تفرضه علينا اللوائح والقوانين في مواقف محددة:**
- I **have to wear** the school uniform. (I have no choice.)
- As employees, we **have to be** at our desks before nine.

- يمكن استخدام (have / has + to + inf.) في المضارع والمستقبل:
- I **have to take** my driving test today. - I **have to take** my driving test tomorrow.

**3) صيغة الماضي لـ (have to / has to / must + inf.) هي (had to + inf.):**
- Rokaya **had to return** home early. (إثبات)
- Ashraf **didn't have to attend** yesterday's meeting. (Not: hadn't to) (نفي)
- **Did** Reem **have to do** any more exercises? (Not: Had Reem...) (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- Where **did** Ayman **have to park** his car? (Not: Where had ...) (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

curriculum_chunks.heading: 6 have to / has to + inf. يجب أن / من الضروري أن

curriculum_chunks.content:
يجب أن / من الضروري أن

- هذه الصيغة شائعة الاستخدام بدلاً من (have to / has to + inf.) في الإنجليزية البريطانية:

$\rightarrow$ He / She / It + has got to + inf. ....

- He has got to attend today's lecture. (إثبات)
- She hasn't got to take any medicines. (نفي)
- Has he got to take extra courses? (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- When has she got to meet the manager? (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

$\rightarrow$ I / We / You / They + have got to + inf. ....

- We have got to water the trees soon. (إثبات)
- They haven't got to work at weekends. (نفي)
- Have we got to finish the project today? (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- What have I got to do to be accepted for the job? (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

- لاحظ صيغة النفي:

$\rightarrow$ haven't / hasn't + got to + inf. ....

- You don't have got to leave now. 
- You haven't got to leave now. 

- لاحظ أنه لا توجد ماضي صيغة من (have/ has + got to + inf.):
- Esraa had got to do the shopping. 
- Esraa had to do the shopping.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 7 have / has + got to + inf.

curriculum_chunks.content:
يجب أن / من الضروري أن

تُستخدم (need / needs + to + inf.) للتعبير عن الضرورة في المضارع والمستقبل:

$\rightarrow$ He / She / It + needs to + inf. ....

- Amr needs to work hard at school to pass the exams. (إثبات)
- Nada doesn't need to do the shopping. = Nada needn't do the shopping. (نفي)
- Does Omar need to carry all these books to school? (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- Why do you need to buy all these groceries? (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

$\rightarrow$ I / We / You / They + need to + inf. ....

- We need to prepare a big lunch for our guests. (إثبات)
- They don't need to pay any more money. = They needn't pay any more money. (نفي)
- Do I need to go to the office every day? (سؤال بـ «هل»)
- When do you need to travel to Aswan? (سؤال بأداة استفهام)

<!-- بداية الصفحة 258 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 8 need / needs + to + inf.

curriculum_chunks.content:
ليس من الضرورى أن

- تستخدم (needn't + inf.) للتعبير عن عدم الضرورة في المضارع:
- Nada needn't do the shopping. Her mum will do it.
= Nada doesn't need to do the shopping. (Not : needn't to ...)
= Nada doesn't have to do the shopping. (Not : needn't to ...)
curriculum_chunks.heading: needn't + inf.

curriculum_chunks.content:
لم يكن من الضرورى أن ...

- تستخدم (needn't have + p.p.) للتعبير عن قيام الفاعل بعمل شيء في الماضي رغم أن ذلك لم يكن ضروريا (الفاعل لم يكن يعرف أن ذلك غير ضروري):
- I needn't have bought a newspaper. My grandpa had already bought one.
- My uncle needn't have bought me chocolate. I have a box in the fridge.
- تستخدم (didn't need to / didn't have to + inf.) للتعبير عن أن الفاعل لم يقم بالفعل لأنه كان يعلم أنه غير ضروري:
- It was sunny and warm, so I didn't need (have) to wear my jacket.
curriculum_chunks.heading: needn't have + p.p.

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. يمكن التعبير عن الضرورة في المستقبل باستخدام:
- ...... must / have to / has to / need to + inf. ...
- ...... will + have / need + (to + inf.) ...
- I must look after my baby sister tomorrow.
- Aya has to do her best at tomorrow's interview to get the job.
= Aya will have to do her best at tomorrow's interview to get the job.

2. تستخدم كل من (must) و (have / has to) للتعبير عن الضرورة أو الإلزام، ويمكن استخدام أحدهما مكان الأخرى مع اختلاف المعنى:
- You must arrive at work on time.
في المثال السابق، تفهم أن المتحدث لديه سلطة الإلزام ويمكن أن يكون المدير أو صاحب العمل.
- You have to arrive at work on time.
في المثال السابق، تفهم أن المتحدث يخضع عن الالتزام بقانون العمل وليس من يملك سلطة الإلزام.

3. تستخدم (have / has to + inf.) للتعبير عن الالتزام بالقانون في مواقف محددة (وليس القانون بوجه عام):
- You have to wear a helmet if you're going to ride your motorbike.

4. تستخدم (must) وليس (have / has to) في القوانين والتعليمات المكتوبة:
- Everyone must turn off mobile phones during duty hours.

5. لاحظ الفرق بين (mustn't) و (don't / doesn't have to):
- You mustn't park here. (ممنوع أو غير مسموح لك أن تركن سيارتك هنا)
= You aren't allowed to park here.
- You don't have (need) to park here. (لست مضطرا لركن سيارتك هنا لكن يمكنك ذلك إن أردت)
= You have the choice to park here or not.

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Marcus:** Welcome back to Green Futures. I'm joined today by Dr. Layla Hussain, energy economist and clean energy supporter. Today, we're focusing mainly on the success stories and the potential of the energy transition really celebrating what's working. Dr. Hussain, let's start with the basics. Which renewable energy source is **leading the charge**$^{(1)}$ right now?

**Dr. Hussain:** Solar, without question. Solar energy is currently the **fastest growing**$^{(2)}$ renewable source worldwide. And the cost of solar panels has fallen by nearly ninety percent in the last decade. That means that in many countries, renewable energy is now actually cheaper than **fossil fuels**$^{(3)}$. Wind and solar together now provide a **significant share**$^{(4)}$ of global electricity, and that share is growing every year.

**Marcus:** So, what are the real-world success stories you find most encouraging?

**Dr. Hussain:** There are many. Take Denmark—a country that has successfully **transitioned**$^{(5)}$ to generating over sixty percent of its electricity from wind! And importantly, this transition has created thousands of new jobs in engineering, manufacturing and maintenance. The idea that moving to renewables means losing employment is simply not true. In fact, the opposite is happening. Developing nations are also increasingly **leapfrogging**$^{(6)}$ fossil fuels entirely and moving straight to renewables, which is extraordinary. **Green hydrogen**$^{(7)}$ is also emerging as a promising solution for heavy industry, where direct **electrification**$^{(8)}$ is difficult.

**Marcus:** What about the challenges? Is battery technology still holding things back?

**Dr. Hussain:** Battery technology was a major **obstacle**$^{(9)}$, but not anymore. Advances in battery storage are rapidly solving the problem of **intermittency**$^{(10)}$, the fact that the sun and wind are not constant. Storage is the real **game-changer**$^{(11)}$ here. I should also add that this transition requires both public and private **investment**$^{(12)}$ working together; public investment alone is simply not enough. We need businesses, governments, and international institutions all **committed**$^{(13)}$. And on that note, I must be honest: not all governments have committed to a fully renewable future yet. That remains one of our biggest political challenges.

curriculum_chunks.content:

curriculum_chunks.content:

curriculum_chunks.content:
**What is an adverb ? ما هو الظرف/الحال ؟**

- It is a word that expresses frequency, time, place, purpose, degree or manner.
- الظرف هو كلمة تعبر عن التكرار أو الزمان أو المكان أو الغرض أو الدرجة أو الطريقة (الكيفية)، ويمكن تلخيص الظروف في الخريطة الذهنية التالية:

**Adverbs**

- **Place**
  - Outside
  - Upstairs
  - Here
  - There
  - Everywhere

- **Frequency**
  - Often
  - Never
  - Always
  - Sometimes

- **Time**
  - Afterwards
  - Before
  - Yet
  - Still
  - Later

- **Manner**
  - Well
  - Quickly
  - Carefully
  - Beautifully

- **Purpose**
  - To avoid
  - To get
  - To remember

- **Degree**
  - Very
  - So
  - Extremely

وفيما يلي شرح مبسط لأنواع الظروف:

**1 Adverbs of frequency : ظروف التكرار**

تُستخدم ظروف التكرار للدلالة على درجة تكرار الحدث، وتُستخدم ظروف التكرار التالية قبل جميع الأفعال ما عدا (be) فتأتي بعده:

- always دائماً – usually عادة – often/ frequently غالباً – sometimes أحياناً – occasionally بين الحين والآخر – rarely/seldom نادراً – never أبداً – consistently باستمرار – regularly بشكل منتظم ...etc.

- Mr Nasser **always arrives** at work on time.
- Mr Nasser **is always** at work on time.

وأحياناً تأتي بعض هذه الظروف في بداية أو نهاية الجملة :

- **Sometimes**, Yara prepares the family lunch.
- Yara prepares the family lunch **sometimes**.

وتأتي ظروف التكرار التالية غالباً في بداية أو نهاية الجملة :

- once مرة - twice مرتين - three times - four times (an hour / a day / a week / a month / a year ...etc.)
- every (morning / day / week / year...)

- I get up early **every morning**. = **Every morning**, I get up early.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 272 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Adverbials of Degree and Frequency

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم ظروف الزمان للدلالة على وقت حدوث الفعل، وغالباً تأتي في بداية أو نهاية الجملة وقد تأتي أيضاً بعد الأفعال المساعدة والناقصة، ومن أمثلة ظروف الزمان ما يلي:

today, yesterday, now, still, currently, afterwards, after, before, yet ... etc.

- I haven't done the shopping yet.
- I am sure we met somewhere before.
- She is still doing the shopping.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 Adverbs of time : ظروف الزمان

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم ظروف المكان للدلالة على مكان حدوث الفعل، وغالباً تأتي في بداية أو نهاية الجملة، ومن أمثلة ظروف الزمان ما يلي:

inside, outside, here, there, somewhere, everywhere, outdoors, indoors ...etc.

- I have lived here since I was born.
- The children are playing outdoors.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3 Adverbs of place : ظروف المكان

curriculum_chunks.content:
وهي عبارات ظرفية تبدأ بـ (to + inf.) بمعنى (لكي) وتستخدم للتعبير عن الغرض وتأتي في البداية أو النهاية:

- I follow a strict diet to lose weight.
- To overcome a challenge, you need to work hard.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 Adverbs of purpose : ظروف الغرض

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم ظروف الدرجة لتحديد درجة الصفة، ومن أمثلة ظروف الدرجة ما يلي:

- تماماً – utterly – completely – للغاية – very-extremely – إلى حد كبير so – إلى حد ما quite/rather
- بدرجة كبيرة – greatly – بشكل ملحوظ – significantly – تماماً – absolutely – كلياً – totally
- قليلاً – slightly – بشكل ملحوظ – considerably – إلى حد كبير – largely ...etc.

- The weather is very hot today.
- She is completely exhausted.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 Adverbs of degree : ظروف الدرجة

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم ظروف الكيفية لوصف كيفية حدوث الفعل وهي تمثل إجابة للسؤال بـ (how):

- A: How did Sama write ? B: She wrote clearly.
- A: How does he walk ? B: He walks quickly.

يأتي ظرف الكيفية بعد الفعل أو بعد المفعول:

- A tortoise moves slowly.
- Rodayna spoke to me quietly.

curriculum_chunks.heading: 6 Adverbs of manner : ظروف الكيفية (الطريقة)

curriculum_chunks.content:
١ بصورة عامة يتم تكوين ظرف الكيفية بإضافة (ly) إلى الصفة :

- weak ضعيف – weakly بضعف
- significant ملحوظ – significantly بشكل ملحوظ
- quiet هادئ – quietly بهدوء

٢ وتُضاف (ly) حتى وإن كانت الصفة منتهية بحرف (l) :
- hopeful متفائل – hopefully من المُنتظر
- beautiful جميل – beautifully بطريقة جميلة

٣ الصفة المنتهية بـ (le) يتم حذف حرف (e) وإضافة (y) :
- terrible فظيع – terribly بشكل فظيع

٤ الصفة المنتهية بـ (y) مسبوق بحرف ساكن يتحول إلى (ily) :
- happy سعيد – happily بسعادة

٥ الصفة المنتهية بـ (ly) تتحول إلى ظرف باستخدام (in a ....... way) :

curriculum_chunks.heading: طريقة تحويل الصفة إلى ظرف كيفية

curriculum_chunks.content:
١ hard / hardly

curriculum_chunks.content:
كلمة (good) صفة بينما كلمة (well) ظرف:

| Adjective / adverb | Comparative | Superlative |
|---|---|---|
| good(adj) جيد - صالح - مفيد | better أفضل | best الأفضل |
| well(adj) جيد - صالح - مفيد | better بشكل أفضل | best بالشكل الأفضل |

تُستخدم (good) كصفة (adjective) بمعنى (جيد/صالح/طيب):
- Mr Taha is a good man.

يمكن استخدام (good) كاسم (noun) بمعني الخير:
- Exercise does me good.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 good / well

curriculum_chunks.content:
١ الصفة تصف اسم بينما ظرف الكيفية يصف فعل:
**صفة adjective + noun / ظرف adverb + فعل verb ...**
- She is a good speaker. / She speaks well.
- Amir is a quick runner. / Amir runs quickly.
- Chess is an indoor game. / Chess is played indoors.

٢ بعد أداة الاستفهام (how) نستخدم صفة لوصف اسم ونستخدم ظرف لوصف فعل:
- How good is his behaviour?
- How well does he behave?

٣ يمكن مقارنة الظروف مثل الصفات الطويلة باستخدام:
**more أكثر / less أقل + adv. الظرف + than**
- Sama writes more carefully than Ahmed.
- I drive less quickly than Moataz.

٤ تأتي ظروف الشك / الاحتمال او التكرار قبل الفعل وليس بعده والعكس مع (be):
**usually – probably – possibly – definitely .........**
- It is possible that he will visit us. = - He will possibly visit us.

٥ هناك ظروف يمكن أن تُستخدم لتغير معني الجملة بالكامل وتُسمَّى (Sentence Adverbs) وغالبا تستخدم في بداية الجملة مثل:
Fortunately, / Luckily, – لحسن الحظ – unfortunately, / Unluckily, – لسوء الحظ – Strangely, – بغرابة – Interestingly, – من المثير للاهتمام – Surprisingly, – من المدهش – clearly, – بوضوح – generally, – بوجه عام – currently, – حالياً – arguably, – بل شك – undoubtedly, – من الممكن ان ...
- Luckily, I found my lost keys.
- Strangely, he agreed to help us.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 276 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Important notes on adverbs

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. ... verb + adverb = ... adjective + in / at ... + (inf. + ing)
- She speaks English well. = She is good at speaking English.

2. ... adverb = in + adj. + way / manner.
- His behaviour was friendly. = He behaved in a friendly way.

3. It is + adj. = adverb
- It is strange that she refused the offer.
= Strangely, she refused the offer.

4. ... be + adverb + adj. = have + adj. + noun ......
- I am seriously ill. = I have a serious illness.

5. Subject + never / rarely / hardly / no sooner ... + verb ......
= Never / Rarely / Hardly / No sooner/Little + فعل مساعد + subj. + verb ...
- Mai never went shopping.
= Rarely did Mai go shopping.

curriculum_chunks.content:
In recent years, Egypt has taken important steps to protect the environment and move towards a greener future. One of the most **well-known**$^{(1)}$ projects is the Benban Solar Park, which is one of the largest solar energy projects in the world. It produces clean electricity using sunlight and helps reduce pollution caused by fossil fuels.

Another major **initiative**$^{(2)}$ is the “Go Green Initiative”, launched by the Ministry of Environment. This project aims to raise **awareness**$^{(3)}$ among citizens about protecting **natural resources**$^{(4)}$, reducing plastic use, and **recycling**$^{(5)}$ waste. It encourages people, especially young learners, to take responsibility for their environment.

Egypt is also working on improving cities through the Green Cities Program, which includes projects in Cairo such as waste recycling, clean transportation, and energy **efficiency**$^{(6)}$ in buildings. These projects aim to make cities healthier and more **sustainable**$^{(7)}$ places to live.

In addition, the government and international organizations are supporting recycling projects, especially in **electronic waste**$^{(8)}$. New laws and programs help manage e-waste safely and encourage small businesses to recycle materials instead of throwing them away.

Another example is the development of Sharm El-Sheikh as a “green city”, where hotels use solar energy, and public transport is becoming more **environmentally friendly**$^{(9)}$. These efforts aim to reduce carbon **emissions**$^{(10)}$ and protect natural resources.

These projects show that Egypt is moving towards **sustainability**$^{(11)}$. However, success depends not only on governments but also on individuals who must change their daily habits and support green solutions.

curriculum_chunks.heading: Word Family

curriculum_chunks.content:
Last spring, the Egyptian Youth Environment Network(1) held its annual conference(2) in Cairo. The conference coordinator(3), Ms. Hana Karim, opened the event by saying that she had never seen so much determination(4) from young Egyptians in all her years of environmental work. She added that the solutions to Egypt's environmental challenges(5) were already being developed by students and young innovators(6) across the country.

One inspiring story came from Omar Taha, an engineering student from Cairo University. He told the audience that his team had designed a low-cost(7) solar water heater(8) that could be installed on ordinary rooftops. He explained that the device could reduce a family's electricity bill(9) by up to forty percent. When a journalist asked him whether the technology was affordable(10) for lower-income families, Omar replied that the total cost of materials(11) was less than three thousand Egyptian pounds.

Another memorable(12) moment came from Farida Mustafa, a sixteen-year-old from Luxor. She said that she had started a Nile clean-up campaign(13) with just five friends and that it had grown to over two hundred volunteers(14) within a year. She warned that the river was changing rapidly(15) and that their generation had a responsibility to protect it. She encouraged everyone to take action, however small, in their local community(16).

As the conference closed, Ms. Karim reminded the delegates(17) that Egypt was specially positioned to lead environmental innovation(18) in Africa. She told the young participants that the decisions their generation made in the coming years would shape(19) the future of the country and the planet.

curriculum_chunks.content: ١ تبدأ عبارات الوصل بأحد ضمائر/ظروف الوصل التالية: **who, whom, which, that, where, when, whose, what** e.g. Relative pronoun Relative clause The little girl **who** is playing over there is my daughter. ٢ عبارات الوصل تعطي معلومات عن شخص أو شيء أو مكان أو زمن أو سبب أو فكرة: e.g. - I know the man **who/that** looks after the garden. (person) - A lion is an animal **which/that** is endangered. (thing) - Cairo is a city **where** millions of people live.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Getting Started

curriculum_chunks.content: (thing) - Cairo is a city **where** millions of people live. (place) - Do you remember the day **when** we first met? (time) ٣ قد تكون عبارات الوصل تحديدية، (أي إن المعلومات ضرورية لتحديد المقصود وفي هذه الحالة لا نستخدم معها فواصل): e.g. - The bird **which** is on the branch is an eagle. () - The eagle, **which** is a bird, is a symbol of strength. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Getting Started

curriculum_chunks.content: () - The eagle, **which** is a bird, is a symbol of strength. () ٤ قد تكون عبارات الوصل غير تحديدية (أي إن المعلومات إضافية وشائعة ويمكن حذفها دون التأثير على المعنى، وفي هذه الحالة نستخدم معها الفواصل): e.g. - Egypt, **which** has a rich history, attracts tourists. () - Egypt **which** has a rich history attracts tourists. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Getting Started

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Subject**

١. تُستخدم (who/that) بعد اسم عاقل كفاعل، وفي هذه الحالة يأتي بعدها فعل ويمكن حذفها واستخدام الفعل مضافًا له (ing) في المبني للمعلوم أو تصريف ثالث في المبني للمجهول:
e.g. - The nutritionist **who** works at the clinic gave us useful advice. ()
= The nutritionist **working** at the clinic gave us useful advice. ()
e.g. - The baby **who/that** was examined yesterday is still ill. ()
= The baby **examined** yesterday is still ill. ()

<!-- بداية الصفحة 11 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: ١ who/that الذي / التي / الذين / اللاتي (للعاقل)

curriculum_chunks.content:
٢. تُستخدم (**who/that**) كمفعول بعد اسم عاقل، وفي هذه الحالة يأتي بعدها فاعل ويمكن حذفها:
e.g. - The baby **who/that** I examined yesterday is still ill. ()
= The baby I examined yesterday is still ill. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: Object

curriculum_chunks.content:
٣. لا تُستخدم حرف جر قبل ضمير الوصل (**who/that**)، لكن يتم وضعه في المكان المناسب في عبارة الوصل.
e.g. - The doctor to who I spoke recommended more whole grains. ()
= The doctor who I spoke to recommended more whole grains. ()

٢ **whom/that** الذي / التي / الذين / اللاتي (للعاقل)
curriculum_chunks.heading: With prepositions

curriculum_chunks.content:
١. تُستخدم (**whom/that**) بعد اسم عاقل كمفعول، ويأتي بعدها فاعل ويمكن حذفها:
e.g. - The baby whom/that I examined yesterday is still ill. ()
= The baby I examined yesterday is still ill. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: Object

curriculum_chunks.content: ٢. تُستخدم حروف الجر قبل ضمير الوصل (**whom**) وفي اللغة غير الرسمية يمكن وضع حرف الجر في المكان المناسب في عبارة الوصل: e.g. - The doctor to whom I spoke recommended more whole grains. (formal) = The doctor whom I spoke to recommended more whole grains. (informal) ٣. يمكن أن يأتي فعل بعد ضمير الوصل (**whom**) إذا جاء قبلها تعبيرات مثل: ... فعل + whom + of + ... , all , some , ... , two , one e.g.
curriculum_chunks.heading: With prepositions

curriculum_chunks.content: , all , some , ... , two , one e.g. - Two of my many friends are doctors. (whom) = I have many friends, two of whom are doctors. ٣ **which/that** الذي / التي / الذين / اللاتي (لغير العاقل)
curriculum_chunks.heading: With prepositions

curriculum_chunks.content:
١. تُستخدم (**which/that**) كفاعل بعد اسم غير عاقل، وفي هذه الحالة يأتي بعدها فعل ويمكن حذفها واستخدام الفعل مضافًا له (ing) في المبني للمعلوم أو تصريف ثالث في المبني للمجهول:
e.g. – Most animals which/that live in forests eat plants. ()
= Most animals living in forests eat plants. ()
e.g. - The deer which/that was hunted by the lion had a broken leg. ()
= The deer hunted by the lion had a broken leg. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: Subject

curriculum_chunks.content:
٢. تُستخدم (**which/that**) كمفعول بعد اسم غير عاقل، وفي هذه الحالة يأتي بعدها فاعل ويمكن حذفها واستخدام التصريف الثالث (p.p.):
e.g. - The deer which/that you hunted had a broken leg. ()
= The deer you hunted had a broken leg. ()

<!-- بداية الصفحة 12 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Object

curriculum_chunks.content:
تُستخدم حرف جر قبل ضمير الوصل (**which**)، ويمكن أيضًا وضعه في المكان المناسب في عبارة الوصل:

e.g. - This is the tool with which I do a lot of jobs. ()

= This is the tool which I do a lot of jobs with. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: With prepositions

curriculum_chunks.content:
يُمكن أن تُستخدم (**which**) كضمير وصل يعود على معنى الجملة التي تسبقها بالكامل:

e.g. - Students often use screens late at night, which can affect their sleep.

which = the fact that students often use screens late at night.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Sentential relative clause

curriculum_chunks.content:
كما سبق، تُستخدم (**that**) مثل (**who/whom/which**) مع العاقل وغير العاقل، لكن لا يسبقها حرف جر ولا تأتي في الجملة الاعتراضية بعد (،):

e.g. – My friend with that I walk to school is crazy about football. ()

= My friend that I walk to school with is crazy about football. ()

e.g. - Egypt, that is an African country, has a rich history. ()

= Egypt, which is an African country, has a rich history. ()
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 that الذي / التي / الذين / اللاتي (مع العاقل وغير العاقل)

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. نستخدم (**whose**) للتعبير عن الملكية. ويأتي بعدها اسم دائمًا. ويمكن أن تشير إلى العاقل وغير العاقل.

e.g. - Students whose sleep routines are regular often concentrate better.

= The charity whose manager is my mother supports many families.

2. تستخدم (**whose**) عندما نحتاج إلى ربط شخص أو شيء بشيء يخصه.

e.g. - The nutritionist whose advice we followed explained the importance of lean protein.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Rule

curriculum_chunks.content:
3. في الإنجليزية الرسمية، يمكن أن يأتي حرف الجر قبل (**whose + noun**) وهذا التركيب أقل شيوعًا لكنه صحيح:

e.g. -The boy about whose diet the doctor was concerned needs support.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 13 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: With prepositions

curriculum_chunks.content:
4. لا نحذف (**whose**) لأنها تحمل معنى الملكية لكن يمكن استخدام تراكيب تؤدي معنى فشابه مثل:
- ... noun + whose + noun ...
- = ... noun + who/which/that + have/has/had + noun ...
- = ... with + noun ...

**e.g.** - The man **who has** gray hair is my uncle. (**whose**) (**with**)
= The man **whose** hair is gray is my uncle
= The man **with** gray hair is my uncle.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Omission

curriculum_chunks.content:
الافعال لا تُستخدم بعد (**whose**) لكن هناك بعض الأفعال التي تُستخدم كأسماء أيضا مثل:
**answer, attack, call, end, export, help, import, increase, influence, plan, reply, start, stay, support, visit, ...**

curriculum_chunks.heading: Tricky point

curriculum_chunks.content: In today's **fast-changing**$^{(1)}$ world, social media plays a **major role**$^{(2)}$ in **shaping**$^{(3)}$ how **teenagers**$^{(4)}$ think, feel, and see themselves. While it can **inspire**$^{(5)}$ healthy habits and positive change, it can also create **unrealistic expectations**$^{(6)}$ and **pressure**$^{(7)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Social Media and Self-Image

curriculum_chunks.content: Over the past **decade**$^{(8)}$, social media **platforms**$^{(9)}$ have **transformed**$^{(10)}$ from simple **communication tools**$^{(11)}$ into carefully chosen stages where individuals perform carefully **constructed**$^{(12)}$ versions of their lives. For teenagers, who are at a particularly **sensitive**$^{(13)}$ stage of **identity formation**$^{(14)}$, this change carries significant **psychological**$^{(15)}$ results.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: **Research**$^{(16)}$ published by the American Psychological Association in 2023 found that teenagers who spent more than three hours daily on **image-based**$^{(17)}$ platforms such as Instagram and TikTok were twice as likely to report **symptoms**$^{(18)}$ of **low self-esteem**$^{(19)}$ and body **dissatisfaction**$^{(20)}$ compared to those who used social media for less than one hour per day. What makes social media especially powerful, and especially dangerous, is the **mechanism**$^{(21)}$ of social **comparison**$^{(22)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: What makes social media especially powerful, and especially dangerous, is the **mechanism**$^{(21)}$ of social **comparison**$^{(22)}$. Unlike traditional media, where the **gap**$^{(23)}$ between ordinary people and celebrities is obvious, social media has hidden this gap completely. Teenagers are now comparing themselves not only to distant celebrities, but to classmates, acquaintances, and **influencers**$^{(24)}$ who present their lives as easily perfect.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: Psychologists use the term **highlight-reel effect**$^{(25)}$ to describe this phenomenon: what appears online is a selective, filtered, and strategically timed part of reality, yet viewers instinctively treat it as a complete and accurate picture. **Glossary:** 1. سريع التغير 2. دور رئيسي 3. تشكيل 4. مراهقون 5. يلهم 6. توقعات غير واقعية 7. ضغط 8. عقد (عشر سنوات) 9. منصات 10. تحولات 11. أدوات تواصل 12. مبنية / مصنوعة 13. حساسة 14. تكوين الهوية

curriculum_chunks.content: **What is Persuasive Language?** **ما المقصود بلغة الإقناع؟** - Persuasive language is language used to affect the reader's opinion, feelings, or actions. لغة الإقناع هي اللغة التي تستخدم للتأثير في رأي القارئ أو مشاعره أو تصرفاته. - Writers may use strong words to make their ideas sound powerful. They may also use careful words to sound balanced and fair. قد يستخدم الكاتب كلمات قوية ليجعل أفكاره مؤثرة. وقد يستخدم ألفاظ متحفظة ليبدو متوازنًا ومنصفًا. لاحظ المثال التالي: **e.g.** **Strong / Biased:**
curriculum_chunks.heading: لغة الإقناع، والتحيّز، والحياد، والتحفظ في التعبير [تخفيف درجة التأكيد]

curriculum_chunks.content: وقد يستخدم ألفاظ متحفظة ليبدو متوازنًا ومنصفًا. لاحظ المثال التالي: **e.g.** **Strong / Biased:** - Social media destroys teenagers' confidence. **Neutral + Hedging:** - Some studies suggest that social media may affect some teenagers' confidence. **Explanation** - الجملة الأولى قوية جدًا لأنها تستخدم كلمة حادة وهي **destroys** - أما الجملة الثانية فهي أكثر توازنًا لأنها تستخدم: - Some studies suggest - may - affect - some teenagers **Here, we focus on persuasive writing techniques such as:**

curriculum_chunks.heading: لغة الإقناع، والتحيّز، والحياد، والتحفظ في التعبير [تخفيف درجة التأكيد]

curriculum_chunks.content: **Definition (التعريف):** A rhetorical question is a question that does not need a direct answer. It is used to make the reader or listener think. السؤال البلاغي هو سؤال لا يحتاج إلى إجابة مباشرة. يُستخدم لجعل القارئ أو المستمع يفكر. **Examples (أمثلة):** - Do we really need likes to feel valued? - Can a perfect photo show the whole truth? - Should teenagers compare themselves to filtered images? **Effect on reader (التأثير على القارئ):**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. الأسئلة البلاغية (Rhetorical Questions)

curriculum_chunks.content: - Should teenagers compare themselves to filtered images? **Effect on reader (التأثير على القارئ):** Rhetorical questions attract attention and make the topic feel personal. تجذب الأسئلة البلاغية الانتباه وتجعل الموضوع يبدو قريبًا وشخصيًا.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. الأسئلة البلاغية (Rhetorical Questions)

curriculum_chunks.content: **Definition (التعريف):** Intensifiers are words that make an idea stronger. أدوات التقوية هي كلمات تجعل المعنى أقوى. **Common intensifiers (أدوات التقوية الشائعة):** - very جدًا - really حقًا - completely كليًا - absolutely بشكل مُطلق - extremely للغاية - significantly بشكل واضح - utterly تمامًا **Examples (أمثلة):** - Social media can be **extremely** stressful. - Many teenagers feel **very** pressured online. - Filtered photos can **significantly** affect self-image. **Effect on reader (التأثير على القارئ):**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. أدوات التقوية / المكثفات (Intensifiers)

curriculum_chunks.content: - Filtered photos can **significantly** affect self-image. **Effect on reader (التأثير على القارئ):** Intensifiers make the writer's point sound stronger and more emotional. تجعل أدوات التقوية رأي الكاتب أقوى وأكثر تأثيرًا أو عاطفية. **Note (ملحوظة):** Using too many intensifiers can make writing sound exaggerated. الإكثار من أدوات التقوية قد يجعل الأسلوب تبدو مبالغًا فيها.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. أدوات التقوية / المكثفات (Intensifiers)

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Definition (التعريف):** Hedging words make a statement sound careful, balanced, and less absolute. ألفاظ التحوط تجعل الجملة أكثر حذرًا وتوازنًا وأقل قطعية. **Common Hedging Words (ألفاظ التحوط الشائعة):** may, might, could, some, many, certain, suggest, appear to, seem | Examples | • Social media **may** affect teenagers' self-image.
• Some posts **might** create unrealistic expectations.
• Certain types of content **could** increase pressure. | |---|---|
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. ألفاظ التحفظ في التعبير (تخفيف درجة التأكيد) (Hedging words)

curriculum_chunks.content:
| |---|---| | Effect on reader | Hedging makes writing sound fair, careful, and academic.
يجعل التحفظ في التعبير الكتابة تبدو منصفة وحذرة وأكاديمية.
**Important Note** **ملحوظة مهمة**
Hedging does not make the writer weak. It shows that the writer is careful and avoids exaggeration.
التحفظ في التعبير لا يعني أن الكاتب ضعيف. بل يدل على أن الكاتب حذر ويتجنب المبالغة. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. ألفاظ التحفظ في التعبير (تخفيف درجة التأكيد) (Hedging words)

curriculum_chunks.content:
| Definition | Absolute words express complete certainty. They leave little or no room for exceptions.
الكلمات القطعية تعبر عن اليقين الكامل، ولا تترك مجالاً كبيراً للاستثناءات. | |---|---| | Common absolute Words | always, never, everyone, all, no excuses, completely, every | | Examples | • Social media **always** harms teenagers.
• **Everyone** compares themselves online.
• There are **no excuses** for unhealthy habits. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 Absolute Words الكلمات القطعية

curriculum_chunks.content:
| | Effect on reader | Absolute words can make writing sound powerful and confident, but they may also make it sound biased or exaggerated.
قد تجعل الكلمات القطعية الكتابة قوية وواثقة، لكنها قد تجعلها أيضاً متحيزة أو مبالغاً فيها. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 Absolute Words الكلمات القطعية

curriculum_chunks.content:
| Definition | Biased language shows an unfair or one-sided opinion.
اللغة المتحيزة تُظهر رأياً غير عادل أو من جانب واحد. | |---|---| | Examples | • Social media always has negative effects on teenagers.
• Online posts are completely unreliable.
• Every influencer presents an unrealistic picture of life. | | Effect on reader | **Why is this biased?** **لماذا تُعد هذه اللغة متحيزة؟**
These sentences make unfair generalizations.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 Biased Language اللغة المتحيزة

curriculum_chunks.content:
They do not allow for different situations or balanced opinions.
هذه الجمل تعمم بشكل غير عادل، فهي لا تترك مجالاً لاختلاف الحالات أو الآراء المتوازنة. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 Biased Language اللغة المتحيزة

curriculum_chunks.content:
| | | |---|---| | **Definition** | Neutral language is balanced, objective, and free from unfair judgment.
اللغة المحايدة هي لغة متوازنة وموضوعية وخالية من الحكم غير العادل. | | **Examples** | • Some teenagers may be affected by social media.
• Certain online posts can create pressure.
• Some influencers present carefully selected versions of their lives. | | **Effect on reader** | Neutral language makes writing sound fair, balanced, and more believable.
تجعل اللغة المحايدة الكتابة أكثر إنصافًا وتوازنًا ومصداقية. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: اللغة المحايدة

curriculum_chunks.content:
| Biased / Too Strong
متحيزة / قوية جدًا | Neutral + Hedging
محايدة مع تحفظ | |---|---| | Social media **destroys** teenagers' confidence. | **Some** studies **suggest** that social media **may affect some** teenagers' confidence. | | **All** teenagers **believe everything** they read online. | **Some** teenagers **may trust** online content without checking it carefully. | | **Influencers are misleading.** | **Some** influencers **may** present carefully selected versions of their lives. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: اللغة المتحيزة مقابل اللغة المحايدة مع التحفظ في التعبير

curriculum_chunks.content: | **Influencers are misleading.** | **Some** influencers **may** present carefully selected versions of their lives. | | Social media is **completely harmful.** | **Certain types of** social media content **could have** negative effects. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: اللغة المتحيزة مقابل اللغة المحايدة مع التحفظ في التعبير

curriculum_chunks.content:
**To make a biased sentence more neutral:**
**لجعل الجملة المتحيزة أكثر حيادًا:**

1. Remove unfair generalizations.
   احذف التعميمات غير العادلة.
2. Replace emotional words with objective words.
   استبدل الكلمات العاطفية بكلمات موضوعية.
3. Add hedging words.
   أضف كلمات تحوّط.
4. Make the sentence more balanced.
   اجعل الجملة أكثر توازنًا.
curriculum_chunks.heading: كيف نعيد صياغة الجمل المتحيزة؟

curriculum_chunks.content:
- Persuasive writing is not only about what the writer says. It is also about how the writer says it.
  الكتابة الإقناعية لا تعتمد فقط على ما يقوله الكاتب، بل تعتمد أيضًا على الطريقة التي يقول بها ذلك.
- A good writer can use strong language to persuade, but can also use neutral and hedging language to sound fair and balanced.
  الكاتب الجيد يستطيع استخدام لغة قوية للإقناع، لكنه يستخدم أيضًا لغة محايدة ومتحوّطة ليبدو منصفًا ومتوازنًا.

curriculum_chunks.content: تبدأ هذه العبارات بـ (V-ing)، وتُستخدم في حالة المبني للمعلوم، ويمكن أن تُستخدم بدلًا من الروابط التالية: **1** While / As + active clause مبني للمعلوم $\rightarrow$ = V-ing. - While I was walking in the street, I lost my keys. $\rightarrow$ Walking in the street, I lost my keys. **2** When + active clause مبني للمعلوم $\rightarrow$ = V-ing. - When I opened the door of the room, I realised that Ahmed was asleep.

curriculum_chunks.content: - When I opened the door of the room, I realised that Ahmed was asleep. $\rightarrow$ Opening the door of the room, I realised that Ahmed was asleep. **3** After / As soon as / Once + active clause مبني للمعلوم $\rightarrow$ = V-ing. - As soon as Sama arrives home, she takes a rest. $\rightarrow$ Arriving home, Sama takes a rest. **4** Because + active clause مبني للمعلوم $\rightarrow$ = V-ing. - Because I was very ill, I didn't go to school.

curriculum_chunks.content: Modern life moves faster than ever. **Technology**$^{(1)}$ saves us time, yet we fill that time with more tasks, screens, and **pressure**$^{(2)}$. How we choose to live – our daily **habits**$^{(3)}$, our **diet**$^{(4)}$, and our sleep – shapes not only our **physical health**$^{(5)}$, but also our **identity**$^{(6)}$ and **sense of self**$^{(7)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Exploring Modern Lifestyles

curriculum_chunks.content: Health experts regularly recommend that teenagers do at least 60 minutes of **moderate**$^{(8)}$-to-hard physical activity every day. This doesn't necessarily mean competitive sport. Activities such as cycling to school, swimming, or even a **brisk**$^{(9)}$ walk, all count towards the daily target. What makes exercise particularly powerful is its effect on the brain: physical activity causes the release of **endorphins**$^{(10)}$, chemicals that reduce feelings of stress and **anxiety**$^{(11)}$ at the same time as boosting mood and **self-confidence**$^{(12)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. Exercise and Physical Activity

curriculum_chunks.content: Furthermore, teenagers who exercise regularly tend to sleep more deeply and report higher levels of **concentration**$^{(13)}$ during school hours. Despite these well-documented benefits, a landmark WHO-led study found that more than 80% of teenagers worldwide fail to meet the recommended daily activity levels, largely due to **sedentary**$^{(14)}$ screen-based habits.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. Exercise and Physical Activity

curriculum_chunks.content: A balanced diet is widely seen as the foundation of physical and mental well-being. **Nutritionists**$^{(15)}$ advise that teenagers consume a varied range of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats, while limiting their intake of **processed foods**$^{(16)}$, too much sugar, and high-caffeine drinks. Poor nutrition has been directly linked to fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and mood changes, all of which affect academic performance. Sleep is equally important, but it is often underestimated.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Nutrition, Sleep, and Recovery

curriculum_chunks.content: Sleep is equally important, but it is often underestimated. Teenagers require from eight to ten hours of sleep per night to support brain development, emotional control, and physical **recovery**$^{(17)}$. Research published in the journal *Sleep Medicine* found that teenagers who slept fewer than seven hours per night were more likely to report symptoms of anxiety and depression. Setting up a regular bedtime routine, such as avoiding screens for one hour before sleeping, has been shown to improve sleep quality. (1) التكنولوجيا (2) ضغط
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Nutrition, Sleep, and Recovery

curriculum_chunks.content: (1) التكنولوجيا (2) ضغط (3) عادات (4) نظام غذائي (5) صحة بدنية (6) هوية (7) إحساس بالذات (8) معتدل (9) سريع (10) إندورفين (11) قلق (12) ثقة بالنفس (13) تركيز (14) قليل الحركة (15) أخصائيون تغذية (16) أطعمة مصنعة (17) تعاف / استشفاء <!-- بداية الصفحة 33 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Nutrition, Sleep, and Recovery

curriculum_chunks.content: In recent years, **mindfulness**$^{(18)}$ has moved from specialist wellness programs into common education. Mindfulness involves paying deliberate attention to the present moment, and can take many forms: meditation, slow breathing exercises, yoga, or simply sitting quietly without a device. Studies suggest that even ten minutes of daily mindfulness practice leads to **measurable**$^{(19)}$ reductions in stress hormones over a period of four to six weeks. Alongside mindfulness, social connection plays a very important role in emotional health.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Mindfulness, Social Connection, and Mindful Consumption

curriculum_chunks.content: Alongside mindfulness, social connection plays a very important role in emotional health. Spending quality time with friends and family — face to face rather than through screens — has been shown to reduce loneliness and build the emotional **resilience**$^{(20)}$ needed to cope with life's pressures. Finally, many psychologists advise us to be conscious not only of what we eat, but also of the media, products, and information we absorb daily. $^{(18)}$ يقظة ذهنية $^{(19)}$ قابلة للقياس $^{(20)}$ مرونة <!-- بداية الصفحة 34 -->

curriculum_chunks.heading: Analytical Paragraph

curriculum_chunks.content:
An analytical paragraph presents a clear claim, explains the reason behind it, supports it with evidence, and shows how the evidence proves the claim.
تعرض الفقرة الإنشائية التحليلية رأيًا واضحًا، وتشرح سببه، وتدعمه بدليل، ثم توضح كيف يبرهن الدليل على الرأي.

An analytical paragraph is used to answer a question, explain a viewpoint, support an opinion, and show understanding through evidence and explanation.
وتُستخدم الفقرة الإنشائية التحليلية للإجابة عن سؤال وشرح وجهة نظر ودعم رأي وإظهار الفهم من خلال الدليل والشرح.
curriculum_chunks.heading: What is an analytical paragraph

curriculum_chunks.content: الأجزاء الرئيسية للفقرة التحليلية
curriculum_chunks.heading: Main Parts of an Analytical Paragraph

curriculum_chunks.content:
الجملة الابتدائية

- Start with a clear opinion that answers the question.
ابدأ برأي واضح يجيب عن السؤال.

**Example**
Physical activity is more influential than diet in improving overall well-being.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Topic Sentence / Claim

curriculum_chunks.content:
السبب

Explain why you believe your claim is well supported.
اشرح لماذا تعتقد أن رأيك مدعوم جيدًا بالأدلة.

**Example**
This is because exercise directly affects both physical health and mental well-being.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 Reason

curriculum_chunks.content:
الدليل

Support your idea using information from the text, examples, or facts.
ادعم فكرتك بمعلومات من النص أو أمثلة أو حقائق.

**Example**
According to the text, physical activity releases endorphins which reduce stress and improve mood.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 35 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3 Evidence

curriculum_chunks.content:
Explain how your evidence supports your claim.

اشرح كيف يدعم دليلك رأيك.

**Example**

This shows that exercise not only improves physical health but also has a strong impact on mental well-being.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 Explanation الشرح

curriculum_chunks.content:
End by reinforcing your main idea.

اختم بتعزيز فكرتك الرئيسية.

**Example**

Therefore, physical activity plays a more significant role than diet in shaping overall well-being.

curriculum_chunks.heading: Don't mix

curriculum_chunks.content: People have different opinions about who is responsible for a person's lifestyle and well-being. Some believe that individuals should make their own healthy choices and take control of their habits. Others argue that family, society, money, and social media strongly **influence**(1) people's decisions. The article explores different **perspectives**(2) on responsibility, **well-being**(3), and the factors that shape human **behavior**(4) and identity.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Whose Responsibility Is It?

curriculum_chunks.content: Many health professionals and philosophers argue that personal responsibility lies at the heart of a well-lived life. From this perspective, every individual possesses the **agency**(5) — the capacity to choose and act, and it is through the exercise of this agency that **identity**(6) is formed. Choosing to exercise, to eat nutritiously, to sleep well, and to manage stress are not simply habits; they are expressions of who we are and what we value.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. The Case for Personal Responsibility

curriculum_chunks.content: Psychologists refer to this as having an "internal **locus of control**(7)" – a belief that one's own actions, rather than external forces, determine outcomes. Research often supports the benefits of taking personal ownership. A **landmark study**(8) published in the Journal of Health *Psychology* found that individuals who scored highly on **self-efficacy**(9) measures – that is, those who believed in their ability to make positive changes – were significantly more likely to maintain healthy **behaviors**(10) over time, regardless of their **socioeconomic background**(11).
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. The Case for Personal Responsibility

curriculum_chunks.content: Furthermore, advocates of personal responsibility argue that framing health as someone else's problem can be **disempowering**(12). When individuals attribute their choices entirely to **outside forces**(13), they risk becoming passive. Taking ownership, by contrast, builds confidence, **resilience**(14), and a sense of purpose, qualities that are central to a positive identity.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. The Case for Personal Responsibility

curriculum_chunks.content: However, the idea that individuals are entirely responsible for their own health is increasingly challenged by social scientists and public health experts. Research in **sociology**(15) demonstrates that where we grow up, how much money our family has, and the cultural rules we are raised with profoundly shape the choices available to us. **Glossary:** 1. يؤثر في 2. وجهات نظر 3. رفاهية / عافية 4. سلوك 5. قدرة على الاختيار والتصرف 6. هوية 7. موضع التحكم 8. دراسة بارزة 9.
