curriculum_chunks.content: 5. قدرة على الاختيار والتصرف 6. هوية 7. موضع التحكم 8. دراسة بارزة 9. كفاءة ذاتية 10. سلوكيات 11. خلفية اجتماعية اقتصادية 12. مضعف للقدرة 13. قوى خارجية 14. مرونة 15. علم الاجتماع <!-- بداية الصفحة 45 --> A teenager growing up in a **neighborhood**$^{(16)}$ with no safe parks or affordable sports facilities cannot simply "choose" to exercise easily. A family with **limited income**$^{(17)}$ may struggle to prioritize fresh vegetables over cheaper processed foods.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Social and Environmental Influences

curriculum_chunks.content: A family with **limited income**$^{(17)}$ may struggle to prioritize fresh vegetables over cheaper processed foods. These are not failures of **willpower**$^{(18)}$; they are **structural barriers**$^{(19)}$, obstacles built into the environment that restrict **genuine choice**$^{(20)}$. Moreover, advertising and social media exert enormous pressure on young people. Brands invest billions in campaigns designed to shape **preferences**$^{(21)}$ and habits, often targeting **teenagers**$^{(22)}$ who are at a particularly **impressionable**$^{(23)}$ stage of development.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. Social and Environmental Influences

curriculum_chunks.content: A third perspective argues that responsibility is not an either-or choice; it does not belong entirely to the individual or entirely to society, but is shared. Governments, schools, families, and communities all have a role in creating the conditions that make healthy living possible and **accessible**$^{(24)}$. In recent decades, many governments have introduced public health **policies**$^{(25)}$ intended to guide and encourage better choices: taxes on high-sugar drinks, restrictions on junk food advertising near schools, and national campaigns promoting physical activity.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. The Role of Government and Shared Responsibility

curriculum_chunks.content: Proponents argue that these **measures**$^{(26)}$ do not remove individual freedom – they reshape the environment so that the healthier choice becomes the easier choice. Economist Richard Thaler's concept of the "**nudge**"$^{(27)}$ captures this idea precisely: small, well-designed changes to the **context**$^{(28)}$ in which decisions are made can shift behavior without restricting freedom. From this viewpoint, responsibility is not abandoned by the individual — it is supported and shared by the **structures**$^{(29)}$ around them. | | | |---|---|

curriculum_chunks.content: الحالة الأولى **Statement** الجملة الخبرية If/Unless + مضارع بسيط , .... will / can / may + inf. .... ex. - If he works hard, he'll pass the next exam. = He'll pass the next exam if he works hard. **Yes / No Q.** السؤال بـ (هل) Will/Can/May + subj. + inf. .... + if + مضارع بسيط ... ? ex. - Will he pass the next exam if he works hard?
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 First conditional

curriculum_chunks.content: ? ex. - Will he pass the next exam if he works hard? = If he works hard, will he pass the next exam? **'Wh-' Q.** السؤال بأداة استفهام Q.W. + will/can/may + subj. + inf. .... + if + مضارع بسيط ... ? ex. - What will happen if he works hard? = If he works hard, what will happen?
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 First conditional

curriculum_chunks.content:
1 تعبر الحالة الشرطية الأولى عن مواقف قابلة للحدوث في المستقبل:
ex. - If I have enough money, I will buy a car. (I believe I'll have enough money).

<!-- بداية الصفحة 56 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Important Notes ملاحظات هامة

curriculum_chunks.content: **١ استخدم المضارع البسيط بعد (if) إذا كانت جملة جواب الشرط تتكون من إحدى الصيغ التالية:** (جملة أمر أو نهي) 1. Inf. / Don't + inf. / Never + inf. ............ ex. - Don't eat too much fat if you (want – wanted – had wanted) to lose weight. - If one of your friends (has – had – had had) a problem, help him/her. 2. Let's + inf. ............ ex.
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: 2. Let's + inf. ............ ex. - Let's take a rest and have a drink if you (are – were – had been) tired. 3. ............ had better ('d better) + inf. ............ ex. - You'd better work hard if you (hope – hoped – had hoped) to succeed. 4. ............ would rather ('d rather) + inf. ............ ex. - I'd rather stay at home if the weather (is – was – had been) windy.
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: - I'd rather stay at home if the weather (is – was – had been) windy. **٢ استخدم (will + inf.) في جملة جواب الشرط إذا كان فعل الشرط أحد الصيغ التالية:** 1. If + subj. (would like / would love / would prefer ............) ex. - If you would like to attend the party, I (will go – would go – would have gone) with you. 2. If + subj. + am / is / are + inf.
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: 2. If + subj. + am / is / are + inf. + ing ............ (مضارع مستمر) ex. - She (won't go – wouldn't go – wouldn't have gone) out if she is revising for her exams. 3. If + subj. + have / has + p.p. ............ (مضارع تام) ex. - If he has left home, you (won't be – wouldn't be – wouldn't have been) able to meet him. **٣ لاحظ الفرق بين (if / in case):**
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: **٣ لاحظ الفرق بين (if / in case):** تعني (if) أن الحدث سيقع إذا توفر شرط معين، فإذا لم يتوفر الشرط لن يحدث شيئًا: ex. - I'll stay at home if it rains. (But I won't stay at home if it doesn't rain) تستخدم (in case) بمعنى (في حالة) لتدل على أننا سنقوم بشيء ما تحسبًا لحدوث شيء معين: ex. - I'll stay at home in case it rains. (I'll stay at home because it may rain)
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: **٢ يمكن أن تحل (can - may - might - must - should) محل (will) في جملة جواب الشرط في الحالة الشرطية الأولى - لاحظ المثال التالي:** ex. - If I feel hungry at work, I will have a snack. (sure متأكد) - If I feel hungry at work, I may have a snack. (probably من المحتمل) - If I feel hungry at work, I might have a snack. (possibly من الممكن)
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: - If I feel hungry at work, I might have a snack. (possibly من الممكن) - If I feel hungry at work, I must have a snack. (necessity ضرورة) - If you can't do the job, you should apologize. (advice نصيحة أو اقتراح suggestion) - If I feel hungry at work, I can have a snack. (ability / possibility قدرة / إمكانية) **٣ لا نستخدم المستقبل بعد (if) مباشرة لكن نستخدم المضارع البسيط:** ex.
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: **٣ لا نستخدم المستقبل بعد (if) مباشرة لكن نستخدم المضارع البسيط:** ex. - If I (will follow - follow) a diet, I will get fit. - What will you buy if you (have – will have) a million dollars? <!-- بداية الصفحة 57 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: الحالة الثانية **Statement** الجملة الخبرية `If/Unless` + (ماضي بسيط (تصريف ثان)) , `would/could/might` + inf. **ex.** - If he trained hard, he'd win the match. = He'd win the match if he trained hard. **Yes / No Q.** السؤال بـ (هل) `Would/Could/Might` + subj. + inf. + if + ماضي بسيط ? **ex.** - Would he win the match if he trained hard? = If he trained hard, would he win the match? **'Wh-' Q.** السؤال بأداة استفهام Q.W.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Second conditional

curriculum_chunks.content: = If he trained hard, would he win the match? **'Wh-' Q.** السؤال بأداة استفهام Q.W. + `would/could/might` + subj. + inf. + if + ماضي بسيط ? **ex.** - What would he do if he trained hard? = If he trained hard, what would he do?
curriculum_chunks.heading: Second conditional

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. تعبر الحالة الثانية عن مواقف تخيليه أو غير محتملة الحدوث في الوقت الحاضر والمستقبل:
**ex.** - If he were taller, he'd be good at basketball.

2. إعطاء النصيحة بالصيغة (If I were ...):
**ex.** - If I were you, I would see a doctor. You look very ill.
- لاحظ إمكانية استخدام (were) مع المفرد في حالة التخيل والنصيحة في الحالة الثانية:
**ex.** - Nada is ill today. If she were / was healthy, she would help you.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Important Notes ملاحظات هامة

curriculum_chunks.content: 1. الأفعال (cut – put – hit – shut – read...) لا تتغير عند تصريفها وتغير في الماضي البسيط إذا لم يضاف لها (s) مع (he – she – it): **ex.** - If he shut the farm door, the animals (won't – wouldn't) go out. 2. إذا كان فعل الشرط (had + noun) تكون الجملة ثانية ونختار (would + inf.): **ex.** - If Abdu had a camera, I (will borrow – would borrow – would have borrowed) it from him. 3.
curriculum_chunks.heading: ملاحظات تساعدك على حل سؤال الاختيار من متعدد

curriculum_chunks.content: 3. إذا كان فعل الشرط (had to + inf.) تكون الجملة ثانية ونختار (would + inf.): **ex.** - If we had to work at the weekend, we (will get – would get – would have got) a reward. 4. إذا كان جواب الشرط (would have + noun) تكون الجملة ثانية ونختار ماضي بسيط: **ex.** - If Sama (win – won – had won) the competition, she would have a prize. <!-- بداية الصفحة 58 -->

curriculum_chunks.content:
إذا كان جواب الشرط (would have to + inf.) تكون الجملة حالة ثانية ونختار ماضي بسيط:
- If Omar (spends – spent – had spent) all his money, he would have to borrow.

من الممكن استخدام التصريف الثالث للفعل كصفة:

- If I had written work, I would do it before going to bed.

(السؤال بـ هل)** Would + subj. + have + p.p. + if + had + p.p. ..... ? - Would he have got the prize if he had won the competition? **Wh- Q.

curriculum_chunks.content: A nationwide(1) school health survey(2) done in Egypt in 2023 gathered(3) data from 450 teenagers aged between 14 and 17, drawn from(4) both urban and rural schools across five governorates(5). The study aimed to identify the primary(6) sources of stress(7) among teenagers and to examine(8) the coping strategies(9) they most commonly(10) adopted(11). Its findings show a complex picture of modern teenage life, in which academic pressure(12), digital habits(13), and social expectations(14) interact(15) in ways that are often difficult to separate.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Understanding Mental Health (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: The most significant finding was that 68% of participants(16) reported experiencing moderate(17) to high levels of stress during examination periods. When asked to identify the main causes, students ranked academic pressure first (cited by 82% of respondents(18)), followed by social media comparison(19) (61%), insufficient(20) sleep (57%), and family expectations (49%).
curriculum_chunks.heading: Understanding Mental Health (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Clearly, the study found that teenagers who did regular physical activity(21)—defined as at least 30 minutes of exercise four or more times per week—reported stress levels that were, on average, 34% lower than those of their sedentary(22) peers, even after controlling for(23) academic performance variables. Cultural background also was a significant factor in how teenagers managed stress. Students from families with strong collectivist(24) values were considerably more likely to seek emotional support(25) from parents or siblings when facing difficulties.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Understanding Mental Health (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: In contrast, students from more individualistic(26) household environments tended to rely on(27) individual coping strategies such as listening to music, exercising alone, or spending time in nature. Neither approach was found to be universally more effective; rather, the study suggested that the availability and quality of support networks(28) were the decisive(29) variables. The researchers also noted a significant gap in access(30) to school counseling(31) services between urban and rural institutions(32).
curriculum_chunks.heading: Understanding Mental Health (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: While 74% of urban schools in the sample offered some form of counseling, the figure dropped to 31% in rural schools. The study concluded that targeted(33) mental health support programs in schools could meaningfully reduce stress levels among teenagers.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Understanding Mental Health (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: This research report(1) explores how screen time(2) affects teenagers' mental health(3), self-image(4), and daily life(5). It also examines the benefits of taking breaks(6) from screens and finding a healthy balance(7) between online(8) and offline(9) activities.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Screen Time and Young People

curriculum_chunks.content: Teenagers today spend an average(10) of seven hours a day looking at screens – and that does not include time spent on screens for school. Researchers and parents alike are increasingly concerned(11) about what all this screen time is doing to developing minds. One of the biggest concerns is the effect of social media on teenagers' self-esteem(12). Platforms like Instagram and TikTok present carefully chosen images(13) of people's lives, making it easy for young users to compare themselves negatively to others.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: Studies suggest that heavy social media use(14) is linked to increased feelings of anxiety(15), loneliness(16), and depression(17), particularly among teenagers. **Glossary:** 1. تقرير بحثي 2. وقت استخدام الشاشات 3. صحة نفسية 4. الصورة الذاتية 5. حياة يومية 6. استراحات 7. توازن 8. متصل بالإنترنت 9. غير متصل بالإنترنت 10. متوسط 11. قلقون / مهتمون 12. تقدير الذات 13. صور 14. استخدام مفرط لوسائل التواصل 15. قلق 16. وحدة 17. اكتئاب
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: 13. صور 14. استخدام مفرط لوسائل التواصل 15. قلق 16. وحدة 17. اكتئاب <!-- بداية الصفحة 73 --> This constant **comparison**$^{(18)}$ can lead young people to develop a wrong sense of their own **worth**$^{(19)}$ and **appearance**$^{(20)}$. Experts note that the **pressure**$^{(21)}$ to gain "likes" and followers can make teenagers feel they are never good enough, which may cause them to **withdraw**$^{(22)}$ from real-world social activities.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: Video gaming is another form of screen time that **sparks debate**$^{(23)}$. Many experts point out that gaming can develop **problem-solving skills**$^{(24)}$, **hand-eye coordination**$^{(25)}$, and **teamwork**$^{(26)}$. However, when gaming becomes **addictive**$^{(27)}$ when a person cannot stop even when they want to. It can **interfere with**$^{(28)}$ sleep, schoolwork, and real-world relationships. The World Health Organization officially recognized "**gaming disorder**$^{(29)}$" as a mental health condition in 2019.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Gaming: Passion or Addiction?

curriculum_chunks.content: Research consistently shows that taking regular breaks from screens can improve **mood**$^{(30)}$, **concentration**$^{(31)}$, and sleep quality. Outdoor activities, face-to-face socializing, and creative hobbies all provide benefits that screens simply cannot **replicate**$^{(32)}$. Studies have found that even short periods of time spent in nature or taking part in **physical activity**$^{(33)}$ can significantly reduce feelings of stress and **restore**$^{(34)}$ mental focus.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Benefits of Stepping Away

curriculum_chunks.content: The key message from researchers is not that screens are entirely **harmful**$^{(35)}$ - as they are an **essential**$^{(36)}$ part of modern life - but that balance matters. Young people who set clear **boundaries**$^{(37)}$ around their screen use, such as avoiding phones an hour before sleep or choosing screen-free times during meals, report feeling more in control of their habits and less anxious overall.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Finding Balance

curriculum_chunks.content: **Mindful**$^{(38)}$ screen use, combined with regular physical activity and offline social connections, gives young people the best chance of a healthy, **fulfilling**$^{(39)}$ leisure life. curriculum_chunks.content: Ask anyone who has ever lost themselves in a painting, a song, or a story, and they will tell you: creative activity is unlike anything else. Time slows down, worries fade, and there is only the work in front of you. Psychologists call this state "flow", a condition of complete **absorption**$^{(1)}$ in a meaningful task. Research suggests that even thirty minutes of creative **engagement**$^{(2)}$ per day can measurably reduce levels of the stress hormone **cortisol**$^{(3)}$, offering young people a natural, **accessible**$^{(4)}$ form of emotional recovery.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Psychological Benefits of "Flow"

curriculum_chunks.content: The benefits of creative leisure go far beyond simple relaxation. **Neuroscientists**$^{(5)}$ have found that making art, whether drawing, playing an instrument, or writing, activates multiple regions of the brain. It strengthens neural connections and improves **cognitive**$^{(6)}$ **flexibility**$^{(7)}$. Unlike passive screen-based entertainment, creative activity demands that the brain produce rather than merely consume. In other words, creative hobbies literally make you smarter, and the evidence for this is growing stronger with each **decade**$^{(8)}$ of research.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Creative Hobbies and Cognitive Growth

curriculum_chunks.content: For teenagers, creative arts offer something especially valuable: a space for **authentic**$^{(9)}$ self-expression. During the teenage years, young people are constantly figuring out who they are, who they want to be, and how they fit into the world. Art provides a safe, non-judgemental **arena**$^{(10)}$ for this exploration. In Egypt, traditional art forms such as **calligraphy**$^{(11)}$, arabesque design, music, and storytelling offer additional layers of cultural meaning, connecting young people to their **heritage**$^{(12)}$ while allowing them to understand it in a new and contemporary way.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Self-Expression and Cultural Identity

curriculum_chunks.content: Collaboration is another strong benefit. A school orchestra, a drama production, a street art collective — all of these require young people to listen to each other, and work toward a **shared goal**$^{(13)}$. These are skills that no classroom test can measure, yet employers and universities consistently rank them among the most valuable skills a young person can possess. **Glossary:** (1) الاندماج كامل (2) مشاركة إبداعية (3) كورتيزول (هرمون التوتر) (4) متاح / سهل الوصول (5) علماء الأعصاب (6) معرفي / ذهني
curriculum_chunks.heading: Developing Valuable Collaborative Skills

curriculum_chunks.content: (3) كورتيزول (هرمون التوتر) (4) متاح / سهل الوصول (5) علماء الأعصاب (6) معرفي / ذهني (7) مرونة (8) عقد (عشر سنوات) (9) حقيقي - أصيل (10) مجال - ساحة (11) خط عربي (12) تراث (13) هدف مشترك <!-- بداية الصفحة 86 -->

curriculum_chunks.content: Perhaps most importantly, creative arts teach young people to embrace failure. In art, there is no single correct answer. A painting that does not turn out as planned is not a failure — it is a lesson. A musician who plays a wrong note in a concert learns more from that moment than from any perfect rehearsal(14).
curriculum_chunks.heading: Building Resilience Through Failure

curriculum_chunks.content: Research by Arts Council England showed that young people who regularly engage in creative activities show greater emotional resilience(15) and are more likely to volunteer in their communities, suggesting that the benefits extend far beyond the individual. curriculum_chunks.heading: Important note: ملاحظة مهمة

curriculum_chunks.content: The World Health Organization recommends that young people aged 5–17 should get at least sixty minutes of medium to hard **physical activity**\(^{(1)}\) every day. Yet across the world — and increasingly in Egypt — many teenagers fall far short of this **target**\(^{(2)}\). A 2024 survey conducted by the Egyptian Ministry of Youth and Sports found that fewer than one in three secondary school students met the recommended weekly activity levels.
curriculum_chunks.heading: "Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People" (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: The rise of **inactive lifestyles**\(^{(3)}\), driven by screen time and intense **academic pressure**\(^{(4)}\), has created what some experts call a "movement crisis" among the young. The benefits of regular sport extend well beyond **physical fitness**\(^{(5)}\). Heart health, stronger bones, and **healthy weight management**\(^{(6)}\) are the most obvious advantages, but the psychological and social gains may be even more significant.
curriculum_chunks.heading: "Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People" (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Psychologists have found that young people who **participate**\(^{(7)}\) in team sports show higher levels of **self-esteem**\(^{(8)}\), better **emotional regulation**\(^{(9)}\), and greater social competence than their non-sporting **peers**\(^{(10)}\). Sport teaches young people how to **lose gracefully**\(^{(11)}\), how to support teammates in difficult moments, and how to **persevere**\(^{(12)}\) through difficulty, all life skills of immeasurable value that transfer directly into academic and professional contexts. Access to sport is not the same for everyone.
curriculum_chunks.heading: "Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People" (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Access to sport is not the same for everyone. Some young people have easy access to sports **facilities**\(^{(13)}\), safe places, and support from their families or schools. However, others may not have these **opportunities**\(^{(14)}\) because of cost, location, or lack of resources. This makes it harder for them to take part in physical activity. It is important to find ways to give all young people a **fair**\(^{(15)}\) chance to enjoy sport.
curriculum_chunks.heading: "Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People" (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: The evidence on what makes young people stay active throughout their lives is remarkably consistent: **enjoyment**\(^{(16)}\) is the strongest **predictor**\(^{(17)}\) of long-term participation. When young people are forced into **competitive**\(^{(18)}\) sport they dislike, or when failure is treated **harshly**\(^{(19)}\), they **disengage**\(^{(20)}\). Young people who find sports they genuinely love — whether competitive or enjoyable, individual or team-based — are far more likely to remain active into **adulthood**\(^{(21)}\).
curriculum_chunks.heading: "Moving More: Why Sport Matters for Young People" (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: The challenge for educators and families is therefore to **expand**\(^{(22)}\) the range of sporting options available, so that every student can find their own movement and carry it with them through life. **Vocabulary List:** 1. نشاط بدني 2. هدف 3. أنماط حياة خاملة 4. ضغط أكاديمي 5. لياقة بدنية 6. إدارة الوزن الصحي 7. يشارك 8. تقدير الذات 9. ضبط الانفعالات 10. أقران / زملاء 11. يخسر بروح رياضية 12. يثابر 13. مرافق 14.

curriculum_chunks.content: When we face unexpected situations outdoors(1), we often learn lessons that contribute to(2) our personal experience(3) and mental growth(4). For instance, being caught in a sudden rainstorm(5) or navigating a difficult trail(6) forces us to be fully present in the moment. This shift in focus(7) moves us away from daily stressors(8) and towards the immediate environment. Ultimately, overcoming(9) these obstacles(10) provides a sense of excitement and achievement that makes the experience truly meaningful(11).
curriculum_chunks.heading: Not Exactly a Relaxing Day

curriculum_chunks.content: My idea of leisure(12) was simple: stay at home, watch a series, and do absolutely nothing. I used to believe that the best way to spend a free day was in complete stillness(13) - a full afternoon on the sofa, curtains(14) half-closed against the afternoon sun, and a cold glass of water on the table beside me. However, my friend insisted(15) that I join him on a cycling trip along the Nile. "It will be relaxing," he said.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: "It will be relaxing," he said. "You'll feel amazing afterwards(16)." I believed him. We started early in the morning, before the city had fully woken up. The air was still cool, the road was quiet, and the Nile shimmered(17) softly beside us. For the first hour, everything felt exactly as promised. We cycled slowly, enjoying the view of the river, the sound of the water, and the occasional call of birds settling on the bank.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: I even began to think that outdoor activities were not as exhausting as I had always imagined and that my friend had been right all along. Then, things changed. The road became longer and less shaded. The sun, which had been gentle and golden at dawn, grew stronger and more direct as the morning wore on. My energy began to disappear.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: My energy began to disappear. My friend, who clearly had considerably more experience, continued cycling as if nothing had happened, as if the heat were simply decoration and the distance were a minor detail. Meanwhile, I struggled to keep up(18). My legs ached. My breathing was uneven. At one point, I seriously considered giving up and calling a taxi home. But something stopped me.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: But something stopped me. Perhaps it was pride, the unwillingness to admit defeat in front of someone who was making it look so effortless. Or perhaps it was something less comfortable to admit: I was genuinely curious whether I could finish. Step by step, I kept going.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: **Glossary:** 1. في الهواء الطلق 2. يسهم في 3. تجربة / خبرة 4. نمو ذهني 5. عاصفة ممطرة 6. طريق / ممر 7. تركيز 8. عوامل ضغط 9. التغلب على 10. عقبات 11. ذو معنى 12. وقت فراغ 13. هدوء تام 14. ستائر 15. أصر 16. بعد ذلك 17. تلألأ / لمع بريق 18. كافح لمجاراة الآخرين <!-- بداية الصفحة 107 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: 17. تلألأ / لمع بريق 18. كافح لمجاراة الآخرين <!-- بداية الصفحة 107 --> We took short breaks in the shade, drank water, laughed at my complaints, and continued moving forward. Each time I thought about stopping, I took one more **pedal stroke**$^{(19)}$ instead. When we finally stopped, I realized we had cycled much farther than I had expected.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: When we finally stopped, I realized we had cycled much farther than I had expected. I was **exhausted**$^{(20)}$ in a way I had never quite experienced before - a deep, physical tiredness that sat in my legs and shoulders like warm sand. But I was also strangely satisfied. Sitting beside the Nile, drinking cold juice, watching the afternoon light change on the water, I felt a **sense of achievement**$^{(21)}$ that no quiet afternoon at home could ever have given me.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: That day changed my understanding of leisure. It is not always about comfort or doing nothing. Sometimes, the best moments come from **effort**$^{(22)}$, from **pushing past**$^{(23)}$ the point where you wanted to stop, and from discovering — with some surprise — that you were more **capable**$^{(24)}$ than you thought. $^{(19)}$ ضغطة بدال $^{(20)}$ مُرهق $^{(21)}$ شعور بالإنجاز $^{(22)}$ جهد $^{(23)}$ يتجاوز $^{(24)}$ قادر <!-- بداية الصفحة 108 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading Text (2)

curriculum_chunks.content:
A diary entry is a form of autobiographical writing in which one records their personal experience, thoughts, feelings, and observations on a regular basis.
تدوينة اليوميات هي نوع من الكتابة الذاتية يسجل فيها الشخص بتظام تجاربه الشخصية وأفكاره ومشاعره وملاحظاته.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1. Definition of Diary entry

curriculum_chunks.content:
A diary entry serves several functional and psychological roles.
تؤدي كتابة اليوميات عدة وظائف عملية وأدوار نفسية:

* **Purpose الغرض**
  * A "safe" outlet متنفس «آمن» للتعبير عن المشاعر
  * Self-reflection and clarity التأمل الذاتي ووضوح الأفكار
  * Creative growth تنمية الإبداع
  * Stress reduction الحد من التوتر
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2. The purpose of a Diary Entry

curriculum_chunks.content: الأجزاء الرئيسية لمفكرة اليوميات
curriculum_chunks.heading: Main Parts of a diary entry

curriculum_chunks.content: Date and salutation (e.g., Dear Diary, Friday...) Set the scene: where you were, what you had just done. ينبغي أن تتضمن المقدمة التاريخ والتحية. فهي تساعد القارئ على معرفة الزمن والمكان وماذا فعلت. **Useful expressions:** * Dear Diary, * Today was a day I will never forget. * I thought it would be a normal day, but I was wrong. * This morning, I went on a trip with my friend. * At first, I expected the day to be relaxing. **Example:**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Opening المقدمة

curriculum_chunks.content: * At first, I expected the day to be relaxing. **Example:** Dear Diary, Today was not the peaceful free day I had imagined. My friend insisted that I join him on a cycling trip along the Nile, and I agreed although I was not sure it was a good idea. <!-- بداية الصفحة 109 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Opening المقدمة

curriculum_chunks.content: Recount the main events in order using narrative tenses. Include: the first hour (positive), the turning point (difficulty), the decision to keep going. لسرد الأحداث الرئيسية بترتيب زمني مستخدماً زمن السرد، اذكر البداية الإيجابية والصعوبة أو نقطة التحول ثم قرارك بمواصلة ما بدأت. **Useful expressions:** - At first, ... - We started by... - While we were cycling, ... - After we had ridden for an hour, ... - Then, things began to change. - As the morning wore on, ... **Example:**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 The story سرد الأحداث

curriculum_chunks.content: - Then, things began to change. - As the morning wore on, ... **Example:** At first, everything felt calm and enjoyable. The air was cool, the road was quiet, and the Nile shimmered beside us. However, after we had cycled for some time, the sun became stronger and the road seemed much longer.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 The story سرد الأحداث

curriculum_chunks.content: Describe the moment you most wanted to stop. What stopped you? Use Past Continuous to show what was happening around you at that moment. صف اللحظة التي رغبت فيها بشدة في التوقف. ما الذي منعك من الاستسلام؟ استخدم الماضي المستمر لوصف ما كان يحدث حولك في تلك اللحظة. **Useful expressions:** - Then, things changed. - At that moment, I felt ... - The hardest moment came when ... - I almost gave up when ...
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3 Turning point نقطة التحول

curriculum_chunks.content: - The hardest moment came when ... - I almost gave up when ... - I began to wonder if I could continue. - I realized that I had to keep going. **Example:** The hardest moment came when my legs began to ache and my breathing became uneven. I almost gave up, but something inside me refused to stop. I wanted to know whether I was capable of finishing the trip.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3 Turning point نقطة التحول

curriculum_chunks.content: How did it feel when you finally stopped? Use a simile or vivid detail to describe your exhaustion and your satisfaction. صف شعورك عند توقفك أخيراً. استخدم تشبيهاً أو تفاصيل وصفية مؤثرة للتعبير عن إرهاقك وشعورك بالرضا. <!-- بداية الصفحة 110 --> **Useful expressions:** - Finally, ... - In the end, ... - When we stopped, ... - By the end of the day, ... - I felt exhausted but proud. - I was tired, but I felt satisfied. **Example:**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 The ending الخاتمة

curriculum_chunks.content: - I felt exhausted but proud. - I was tired, but I felt satisfied. **Example:** Finally, we stopped beside the Nile. I was completely exhausted, but I felt proud of myself. The cold juice, the quiet water, and the afternoon light made the moment unforgettable.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4 The ending الخاتمة

curriculum_chunks.content: What did this experience teach you about yourself? About leisure? This is the diary's message – make it personal and honest. ماذا علمتك هذه التجربة عن نفسك وعن وقت الفراغ؟ هذا هو المغزى الأساسي من تدوينة اليوميات، لذلك اجعله شخصيًا وصادقًا. **Useful expressions:** - This experience taught me that ... - I learned that ... - Now I understand that ... - I used to think..., but now I believe ... - The day changed my understanding of ...
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 Reflection التأمل الشخصي

curriculum_chunks.content: - The day changed my understanding of ... - I discovered that ... **Example:** This experience taught me that leisure is not always about doing nothing. Sometimes, real enjoyment comes from effort, challenge, and discovery that you are stronger than you thought.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5 Reflection التأمل الشخصي

curriculum_chunks.content: End with a memorable line that captures your key insight. It can be funny, philosophical, or both. اختم بجملة مميزة تعبر عن أهم فكرة أو درس توصلت إليه. يمكن أن تكون الجملة طريفة أو فلسفية أو تجمع بينهما. **Useful expressions:** - What a day! - I will never forget this experience. - It was difficult, but it was worth it. - Maybe I am more capable than I thought. - Not exactly relaxing — but definitely meaningful. **Example:**
curriculum_chunks.heading: 6 Final Sentence الجملة الختامية

curriculum_chunks.content: - Not exactly relaxing — but definitely meaningful. **Example:** It was not exactly a relaxing day, but it was definitely a meaningful one. <!-- بداية الصفحة 111 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 6 Final Sentence الجملة الختامية

curriculum_chunks.content: **Before finishing your diary entry, check that you have:** - I wrote the date at the beginning. كتبت التاريخ في البداية. - I started with a suitable greeting, such as "Dear Diary, ..." بدأت بتحية مناسبة، مثل: «عزيزتي، مذكراتي، ...» - I clearly described a personal experience. قدمت وصفًا واضحًا لتجربة شخصية. - I explained what happened. شرحت ما حدث. - I expressed my feelings and thoughts clearly. عبرت عن مشاعري وأفكاري بوضوح. **Diary Entry Structure ترتيب تدوينة اليوميات**
curriculum_chunks.heading: قائمة مراجعة كتابة اليوميات

curriculum_chunks.content: عبرت عن مشاعري وأفكاري بوضوح. **Diary Entry Structure ترتيب تدوينة اليوميات** Date $\rightarrow$ Salutation $\rightarrow$ Opening $\rightarrow$ Events (story) $\rightarrow$ Turning Point $\rightarrow$ Ending $\rightarrow$ Reflection $\rightarrow$ Final Sentence التاريخ $\leftarrow$ التحية $\leftarrow$ الافتتاحية $\leftarrow$ الأحداث (القصة) $\leftarrow$ نقطة التحول $\leftarrow$ النهاية $\leftarrow$ التأمل $\leftarrow$ الجملة الختامية. <!-- بداية الصفحة 112 -->

This unit explores the concept of identity through how memory and history are created, kept, and sometimes debated in Egypt and the wider world. You will study how places hold shared memories, how museums tell historical stories, and how digital platforms are changing the way historical events are recorded and shared.

Through four integrated lessons, you will build your language proficiency across the four key skills.
curriculum_chunks.heading: الوحدة 3: أصداء الماضي والتاريخ - Unit 3: Echoes of the Past

curriculum_chunks.content: Analyze historical narratives and identify the writer's viewpoint.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Reading

curriculum_chunks.content: Listen to media reports about discoveries, and distinguish between stated and unstated information.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening

curriculum_chunks.content: Present a site analysis, express a clear opinion, and recognize an opposing viewpoint.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Speaking

curriculum_chunks.content: Write a discursive paragraph that weighs different perspectives, uses concession clauses, and supports ideas with evidence.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Writing

curriculum_chunks.content:
You will:
- identify how sites of memory preserve collective identity.
- analyze how museums select and present historical narratives.
- evaluate the role of social media in documenting history.
- examine how viral content shapes historical understanding.
- construct structured arguments using the JRE [Justify, Reason, Evidence] framework.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Content Objectives

curriculum_chunks.content:
You will:
- use prepositional phrases of place and time accurately.
- use concession clauses to demonstrate counter-arguments.
- write a discursive paragraph and a personal landmark analysis.
- take part in structured discussions and presentations.

curriculum_chunks.content: Ancient **monuments**(1) and historical sites play an important role in **preserving**(2) the identity and **heritage**(3) of nations. They reflect the **achievements**(4) of past civilizations and help people understand their history more deeply. Exploring these **landmarks**(5) allows visitors to connect with the past, appreciate cultural values, and learn important lessons that continue to influence society and future generations.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Sites of Memory

curriculum_chunks.content: When I stood at the **entrance**(6) to Karnak Temple Complex in Luxor for the first time, I was not struck by its size although it is truly **enormous**(7), but by its **silence**(8). In the early morning, before the tour groups arrive, the avenue of **ram-headed sphinxes**(9) stretches southward in **near-perfect stillness**(10), each one carved from sandstone that was already **ancient**(11) when Cleopatra walked beside it.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: In the space between the columns, with the first light falling at a low angle across the hieroglyphics, it feels as if time has not moved at all. Karnak is not a single building but a **landscape**(12) of **accumulated**(13) memory. Built over more than two thousand years from the **reign**(14) of Senusret in the Middle Kingdom to the Ptolemaic era - the complex represents the longest continuous building project in human history.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Each pharaoh added, changed, or **inscribed**(15) something, leaving layers of **devotion**(16) and ambition **encoded**(17) in stone. The Hypostyle Hall alone contains 134 **massive**(18) columns, decorated from floor to ceiling. This space was designed not simply to impress but to **communicate**(19): it belonged to the gods, and the pharaoh was their **representative**(20) on earth. **Vocabulary** (1) آثار - صرح (2) صون - حفاظ (3) تراث - إرث (4) إنجازات (5) معالم بارزة (6) مدخل (7) ضخم / هائل (8) صمت - سكون
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: (4) إنجازات (5) معالم بارزة (6) مدخل (7) ضخم / هائل (8) صمت - سكون (9) أبو الهول برأس كبش (10) سكون شبه تام (11) قديم - أثري (12) مشهد - تضاريس (13) متراكم (14) عهد - حكم (15) منقوش (16) تفان - إخلاص (17) مرمز - مشفر (18) ضخم - هائل (19) يتواصل - يبلغ (20) ممثل - نائب
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: <!-- بداية الصفحة 127 --> What I find most **significant**$^{(21)}$, however, is not what has survived, but the question the site invites us to ask as Egyptians today. Karnak was not built for tourists; it was built for a **civilization**$^{(22)}$. Yet as we walk through its vast spaces, we are reminded that history is not only something we observe, but something we **interpret**$^{(23)}$ and **carry forward**$^{(24)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Stones That Remember: A Walk Through Karnak (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: If a site of memory belongs to everyone, how should it be understood, and whose voices should shape the way it is told? These are not **abstract**$^{(25)}$ questions, they are the questions that every Egyptian student standing between those columns should feel encouraged to explore. curriculum_chunks.content:
Good academic and journalistic writing acknowledges counterarguments before addressing them. This is done through concession clauses – they show that the writer is aware of other viewpoints.

تعترف الكتابة الأكاديمية والصحفية الجيدة بالحجج المضادة قبل مناقشتها والرد عليها. ويتم ذلك باستخدام جمل الإقرار بالرأي الآخر؛ فهي توضح أن الكاتب على دراية بوجهات النظر الأخرى.
curriculum_chunks.heading: عبارات التناقض أوالاستدراك (التعبير عما هو غير متوقع) Concession Clauses

curriculum_chunks.content:
Concession clauses are language structures used to introduce an opposing idea politely before presenting your own idea.

جمل الإقرار بالرأي الآخر هي تراكيب لغوية تستخدم لتقديم الفكرة المعارضة بطريقة مهذبة قبل عرض فكرتك أو وجهة نظرك.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 What are concession clauses?

curriculum_chunks.content:
The opposite opinion or idea that argues against your point of view.

الرأي أو الفكرة المعارضة لوجهة نظرك ومن أهم روابط الاستدراك والإقرار بالرأي الآخر

- although, though, even though, despite, in spite of, nevertheless
- however (showing unexpected result)

e.g. - **Although** he studied hard, he failed the exam.
- **Despite** being tired, she continued working.

curriculum_chunks.content: Since the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) opened its doors to the public(1) on 4 November 2025, it has been described as the largest archaeological(2) museum in the world. Located near the famous Pyramids of Giza, the museum covers 45,000 square meters and houses more than 100,000 artifacts(3) from ancient Egypt. Among these treasures is the complete collection of Tutankhamun, displayed together for the first time in history.
curriculum_chunks.heading: A Journey Through Time (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Among these treasures is the complete collection of Tutankhamun, displayed together for the first time in history. The impressive Grand Staircase alone features 87 colossal(4) royal statues, arranged in chronological(5) order, offering visitors a breathtaking introduction to thousands of years of Egyptian civilization. Even though the museum is modern, it presents the story of one of the world's oldest civilizations(6). Designing a museum of this scale is no simple task.
curriculum_chunks.heading: A Journey Through Time (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Designing a museum of this scale is no simple task. Curators(7) must make careful decisions about which objects to display, how to arrange them, and what stories to tell. At the GEM, the journey begins in prehistory and moves forward through the great dynasties(8) of ancient Egypt. This structure helps visitors understand how one of the world's greatest civilizations developed step-by-step over time. Multilingual(9) labels, interactive screens, and guided tours make the experience enjoyable and accessible(10) to Egyptian and international visitors of all ages.
curriculum_chunks.heading: A Journey Through Time (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: One of the most exciting aspects of the GEM is its strong focus on education. School trips, workshops, and special programs(11) are available to students across Egypt, giving young people the opportunity to connect with their heritage(12) in a hands-on and memorable way.
curriculum_chunks.heading: A Journey Through Time (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Although a single museum cannot include every story from Egypt's rich past, the GEM makes a remarkable effort to represent the depth and variety of ancient Egyptian life — from royal tombs and temple art to everyday objects used by ordinary people thousands of years ago. Unlike many museums that are mainly designed for tourists, the GEM plays an important educational role for Egyptian students.
curriculum_chunks.heading: A Journey Through Time (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: The GEM is not only a place to view ancient objects; it is also a space where science and history come together. Conservation(13) laboratories inside the museum allow experts to study and restore(14) artifacts using the latest technology(15), ensuring that these national treasures are carefully preserved(16) for future generations. The collection continues to grow, develop, and surprise its visitors, keeping the museum a dynamic experience for many years to come.

curriculum_chunks.content:
A discursive paragraph is a piece of writing that discusses different ideas or opinions about a topic in a balanced and objective way before reaching a conclusion or expressing a personal opinion.

الفقرة النقاشية هي نوع من الكتابة يعرض آراءً أو وجهات نظر مختلفة حول موضوع معين بطريقة متوازنة وموضوعية، ثم ينتهي برأي شخصي أو استنتاج مناسب.
curriculum_chunks.heading: What Is a Discursive Paragraph?

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. Discussing different viewpoints about a topic. مناقشة وجهات النظر المختلفة حول موضوع ما.
2. Presenting arguments and counterarguments. عرض الحجج والآراء المضادة.
3. Comparing different perspectives. مقارنة الأفكار ووجهات النظر المختلفة.
4. Encouraging critical thinking. تنمية التفكير النقدي.
5. Reaching a balanced conclusion based on evidence and reasoning. الوصول إلى استنتاج متوازن قائم على الأدلة والمنطق.
curriculum_chunks.heading: What is a discursive paragraph used for?

curriculum_chunks.content:
الأجزاء الرئيسية للفقرة النقاشية

A discursive paragraph consists of five main parts as modelled in the lesson.
تتكون الفقرة النقاشية من خمسة أجزاء رئيسية وفقًا لنموذج الكتابة الوارد في الدرس.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Main Parts of a Discursive Paragraph

curriculum_chunks.content:
الجملة الافتتاحية
Introduces the issue or topic clearly. تقدم الجملة الافتتاحية التي سنناقش بوضوح.
- Useful expressions:
Many people have different opinions about preserving history.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Topic Sentence

curriculum_chunks.content:
الرأي الأول / وجهة النظر الأولى
Presents one side of the argument with explanation or examples. يعرض الكاتب وجهة نظر معينة ويدعمها بالتفسير أو الأمثلة.
- Useful expressions:
- On the one hand, ...
- Some people believe that ...
- One argument in favour of ... is that ...

<!-- بداية الصفحة 142 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 First Point / First Perspective

curriculum_chunks.content:
Presents the opposite viewpoint using concession clauses and contrast language.
يعرض الكاتب الرأي المخالف مستخدمًا تراكيب المخالفة وأدوات التباين.
* **Useful expressions:**
  - On the other hand, ...
  - However, ...
  - Nevertheless, ...
  - It may be argued that ...
curriculum_chunks.heading: الرأي المقابل / وجهة النظر الأخرى

curriculum_chunks.content:
Expresses a personal opinion or presents a balanced judgement after considering both sides.
يعبر الكاتب عن رأيه الشخصي أو يقدم رؤية متوازنة بعد مناقشة الرأيين.
* **Useful expressions:**
  - In my opinion, ...
  - From my perspective, ...
  - It seems that ...
  - A balanced approach may be the best solution.
curriculum_chunks.heading: الرأي الشخصي / الرؤية المتوازنة

curriculum_chunks.content:
Ends the paragraph with a final statement that summarises the discussion.
تنهي الفقرة بجملة ختامية تلخص الأفكار الرئيسية التي تمت مناقشتها.
* **Useful expressions:**
  In conclusion, ... / To sum up, ... / Overall, ...
curriculum_chunks.heading: الجملة الختامية

curriculum_chunks.content:
* **Concession Clauses:**
  to acknowledge opposing viewpoints.
  لعرض الرأي المقابل بصورة متوازنة.
* **Prepositional Phrases:**
  to add details and support ideas.
  لإضافة التفاصيل ودعم الأفكار.
curriculum_chunks.heading: التراكيب اللغوية المستخدمة في الفقرة النقاشية

curriculum_chunks.content:
**Although + clause** بالرغم من أن + جملة
- Although museums are expensive to maintain, they preserve valuable heritage.
بالرغم من أن المتاحف تكلف كثيرًا للصيانة، إلا أنها تحفظ التراث الثمين.

**Despite + noun phrase** على الرغم من + اسم
- Despite technological advances, many people still prefer visiting museums in person.

**Prepositional phrases of place & time** شبه الجمل الدالة على المكان والزمان
- In my opinion, museums play an essential role in preserving identity.

curriculum_chunks.content:
1. Topic Sentence (الجملة الافتتاحية)
2. First Point (الرأي الأول)
3. Contrasting Point (الرأي المقابل)
4. Personal Opinion (الرأي الشخصي)
5. Concluding Sentence (الجملة الختامية)

curriculum_chunks.content: To "**go viral**$^{(1)}$" means to spread rapidly and widely online (often within 24 hours). This spread is driven by emotional **engagement**$^{(2)}$ (surprise, pride, or **nostalgia**$^{(3)}$) rather than historical accuracy or truth.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Viral Past

curriculum_chunks.content: Never before in human history have historical images, **artifacts**$^{(4)}$, and **claims**$^{(5)}$ reached many people so quickly. A single post about an Egyptian pharaoh can **accumulate**$^{(6)}$ millions of views within twenty-four hours; a **colorized**$^{(7)}$ photograph of ancient Alexandria can be shared across continents before a single historian has had the opportunity to **verify**$^{(8)}$ its **accuracy**$^{(9)}$. The **scale**$^{(10)}$ and speed of this spread are, in themselves, remarkable. The problem is that scale and speed have no real relationship to truth.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Why Viral History is Not Always True History

curriculum_chunks.content: The problem is that scale and speed have no real relationship to truth. The way social media platforms work increases this risk considerably. These platforms are designed not to **prioritize**$^{(11)}$ accuracy but to promote engagement. Research **consistently**$^{(12)}$ shows that engagement is driven by emotion. **Content**$^{(13)}$ that causes surprise, pride, nostalgia, or strong reaction spreads more **rapidly**$^{(14)}$ than content that is measured, detailed, or carefully **qualified**$^{(15)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Why Viral History is Not Always True History

curriculum_chunks.content: A viral post may claim that the Great Pyramid was built in a single decade by a team of fifty engineers. Such posts often accumulate more shares than carefully sourced corrections. In reality, the actual **construction**$^{(16)}$ process **unfolded**$^{(17)}$ over decades and involved tens of thousands of workers. The **consequences**$^{(18)}$ for our understanding of history are significant.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Why Viral History is Not Always True History

curriculum_chunks.content: The **consequences**$^{(18)}$ for our understanding of history are significant. In Egypt, where the relationship between ancient **heritage**$^{(19)}$ and national identity is particularly important, the viral spread of historical **myths**$^{(20)}$ and false claims risks **distorting**$^{(21)}$ the public's understanding of who they are and where they come from. Rarely do virality and accuracy move in the same direction.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Why Viral History is Not Always True History

curriculum_chunks.content: Rarely do virality and accuracy move in the same direction. curriculum_chunks.content: For most of human history, news of a great **archaeological**$^{(1)}$ discovery traveled slowly. A royal tomb found in the Valley of the Kings might be reported in a **specialist**$^{(2)}$ journal months after the **excavation**$^{(3)}$ began, reaching only a small community of **scholars**$^{(4)}$ and museum professionals. The wider public—whether in Egypt or abroad—would wait years before seeing even a photograph of what had been **uncovered**$^{(5)}$. Knowledge of the past was carefully managed, moving through **official**$^{(6)}$ channels before it reached ordinary people.
curriculum_chunks.heading: How Social Media Is Bringing Egyptian Discoveries to the World. (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Knowledge of the past was carefully managed, moving through **official**$^{(6)}$ channels before it reached ordinary people. Social media has transformed this process in **remarkable**$^{(7)}$ ways. When an exciting find is made today, whether a **sealed**$^{(8)}$ tomb in Luxor, a **submerged**$^{(9)}$ city off the coast of Alexandria, or an ancient **papyrus**$^{(10)}$ in the Delta. It can be photographed, posted, and shared with millions of people within hours.
curriculum_chunks.heading: How Social Media Is Bringing Egyptian Discoveries to the World. (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: It can be photographed, posted, and shared with millions of people within hours. Official accounts run by **organizations**$^{(11)}$ such as the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities now use **platforms**$^{(12)}$ like X and Instagram to **document**$^{(13)}$ discoveries in **real time**$^{(14)}$, allowing **followers**$^{(15)}$ from Cairo to Tokyo to watch history being uncovered. For the first time, Egypt's **extraordinary**$^{(16)}$ **heritage**$^{(17)}$ is being shared with the world at the very moment it is found. There are challenges to consider, however.
curriculum_chunks.heading: How Social Media Is Bringing Egyptian Discoveries to the World. (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: There are challenges to consider, however. A post on X can be deleted; an Instagram story **expires**$^{(18)}$ after twenty-four hours; a TikTok video may be removed by its **creator**$^{(19)}$ or by the platform's **moderation**$^{(20)}$ systems within minutes of going **viral**$^{(21)}$. Unlike a stone **inscription**$^{(22)}$ or a printed journal, social media **documentation**$^{(23)}$ is **fragile**$^{(24)}$. There is also the question of **accuracy**$^{(25)}$: not every post about an Egyptian discovery is published by experts, and images or **claims**$^{(26)}$ can sometimes be **misunderstood**$^{(27)}$ or shared out of context.
curriculum_chunks.heading: How Social Media Is Bringing Egyptian Discoveries to the World. (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Specialists argue that social media is most valuable when it works **alongside**$^{(28)}$ careful **academic**$^{(29)}$ documentation and **preservation**$^{(30)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: How Social Media Is Bringing Egyptian Discoveries to the World. (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: **What is Fronting?** - Fronting means moving a word or phrase to the beginning of a sentence to give it emphasis. - It is used in formal writing and reports to add emphasis. - It also makes your sentences more varied and interesting. $\rightarrow$ Subject + Verb + Object / Complement / Adverbial **e.g.** - Normal: Food waste is a serious problem in Egypt. - Fronting: In Egypt, food waste is a serious problem.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Fronting

curriculum_chunks.content: - Fronting: In Egypt, food waste is a serious problem. - Normal: Bread goes bad quickly as a result of poor storage. - Fronting: As a result of poor storage, bread goes bad quickly. - Normal: I have never seen so much food wasted. - Fronting: Never have I seen so much food wasted. 1. Normal fronting 2. Fronting with inversion
curriculum_chunks.heading: Fronting

curriculum_chunks.content:
| Type | Explanation | | :--- | :--- | | **1. Place phrase** | **FUNCTION:** To emphasize where something happens.
**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Place phrase + comma + subject + V
**e.g.**
Normal: Food waste is a serious problem in Egypt.
Fronting: In Egypt, food waste is a serious problem.
**ADVANCED POINT:** | | **2.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Normal Fronting

curriculum_chunks.content:
| **2. Time phrase** | **FUNCTION:** To emphasize when something happens.
**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Time phrase + comma + subject + V
**e.g.**
Normal: We buy more food than we need during Ramadan.
Fronting: During Ramadan, we buy more food than we need. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 1 Normal Fronting

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم عبارة السبب

**FUNCTION:** To put the reason before the result.
- وضع السبب قبل النتيجة.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Cause phrase + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - Bread goes bad quickly because of poor storage.
Fronting: - Because of poor storage, bread goes bad quickly.

**Important Note:**
$\rightarrow$ because of/due to/as a result of + a noun phrase or gerund
$\rightarrow$ because / as / since + a full clause جملة
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Cause phrase

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم عبارة النتيجة

**FUNCTION:** To emphasize the result or consequence.
- إبراز النتيجة أو الأثر.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Result phrase + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - The weather was bad. As a result, the flight was delayed.
Fronting: - As a result of the bad weather, the flight was delayed.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4. Result phrase

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم عبارة التباين

**FUNCTION:** To show contrast from the beginning.
- إظهار التباين منذ بداية الجملة.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Contrast phrase + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - Egypt grows many crops, unlike some dry countries.
Fronting: - Unlike some dry countries, Egypt grows many crops.

**ADVANCED POINT:** $\rightarrow$ Unlike + a noun phrase
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5. Contrast phrase

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم عبارة أو جملة التناقض

**FUNCTION:** To show an unexpected contrast.
- إظهار فكرة مخالفة أو غير متوقعة.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Concession phrase/clause + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - Some people misunderstand food dates despite clear labels.
Fronting: - Despite clear labels, some people misunderstand food dates.

**Important Note:**
$\rightarrow$ Despite / in spite of + noun or gerund
$\rightarrow$ Although / even though + full clause.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 177 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 6. Concession phrase / clause

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم المفعول به

**FUNCTION:** To emphasize the object.
- إبراز المفعول به.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Object + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - We cannot ignore this problem.
Fronting: - This problem, we cannot ignore.

**ADVANCED POINT:**
Object fronting can sound dramatic or rhetorical, so it should be used carefully.
- قد يبدو تقديم المفعول به خطابيًا أو قويًا جدًا؛ لذلك يجب استخدامه بحذر.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 7. Object fronting

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم شبه الجملة

**FUNCTION:** To present background information first.
- تقديم معلومات تمهيدية مثل المصدر أو الوسيلة أو الموضوع.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Prepositional phrase + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - Food waste can be reduced according to the report.
Fronting: - According to the report, food waste can be reduced.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 8. Prepositional phrase

curriculum_chunks.content: تقديم عبارة اسم الفاعل أو اسم المفعول **FUNCTION:** To make writing shorter and more formal. - جعل الكتابة أكثر اختصارًا ورسمية. **STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ V-ing / past participle phrase + comma + subj. + V e.g. Normal: - Fresh food goes bad quickly when it is stored incorrectly. Fronting: - Stored incorrectly, fresh food goes bad quickly. **ADVANCED POINT:** The subject of the participial phrase must logically match the subject of the main clause.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 9. Participial phrase

curriculum_chunks.content: **ADVANCED POINT:** The subject of the participial phrase must logically match the subject of the main clause. - يجب أن يكون فاعل عبارة اسم الفاعل / اسم المفعول متوافقًا منطقيًا مع فاعل الجملة الرئيسية.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 9. Participial phrase

curriculum_chunks.content:
تقديم عبارة المصدر

**FUNCTION:** To express purpose clearly.
- التعبير عن الغرض أو الهدف بوضوح.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ To + infinitive + comma + subject + V

e.g.
Normal: - Families should plan meals carefully to reduce food waste.
Fronting: - To reduce food waste, families should plan meals carefully.

**ADVANCED POINT:**
This structure is very useful in recommendations and formal reports.
- هذا التركيب مفيد جدًا في التوصيات والتقارير الرسمية.

<!-- بداية الصفحة 178 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 10. Infinitive phrase

curriculum_chunks.content:
التقديم باستخدام

**FUNCTION:** To emphasize the important thing or idea.
- إبراز الفكرة أو الشيء المهم.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ What + subject + V + be + emphasized part

e.g.
Normal: - Many families need better planning.
Fronting: - What many families need is better planning.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 11. What-clause

curriculum_chunks.content:
التوكيد باستخدام

**FUNCTION:** To emphasize a person, thing, time, place, or reason.
- تأكيد شخص أو شيء أو زمن أو مكان أو سبب.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ It + be + emphasized part + that/who + rest

e.g.
Normal: - Poor storage causes food waste.
Fronting: - It is poor storage that causes food waste.

**ADVANCED POINT:**
Use *who* for people and *that* for things, times, places, and reasons.
- نستخدم **who** مع الأشخاص، ونستخدم **that** مع الأشياء والأزمنة والأماكن والأسباب.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 12. It-cleft

curriculum_chunks.content:
التقديم الذي يستلزم تقديم الفعل المساعد على الفاعل | Type | Explanation | | :--- | :--- | | **1. Negative adverbial**
تقديم عبارة منفية | **FUNCTION:** To give strong formal emphasis.
- التأكيد القوي في الأسلوب الرسمي.
**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Negative/restrictive phrase + auxiliary + subj. + V
e.g.
Normal: - I have never seen so much food wasted.
Fronting: - Never have I seen so much food wasted.
**ADVANCED POINT:**
- في زمن المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط نستخدم **do / does / did** عند القلب. | | **2.

curriculum_chunks.content:
| | **2. Only expressions**
التقديم باستخدام Only | **FUNCTION:** To show that something happens only after a condition, time, or method.
- بيان أن شيئًا يحدث فقط بعد شرط أو وقت أو وسيلة معينة.
**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Only + phrase/clause + auxiliary + subject + V
e.g.
Normal: - She understood the date only after reading the label.
Fronting: - Only after reading the label did she understand the date.
**ADVANCED POINT:**
- إذا كانت **only** تصف الفاعل نفسه، فلا يحدث تقديم للفعل المساعد.
e.g. - Only careful planning can reduce waste. |
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 Fronting with inversion

curriculum_chunks.content: - Only careful planning can reduce waste. | <!-- بداية الصفحة 179 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 2 Fronting with inversion

curriculum_chunks.content: التقديم باستخدام **FUNCTION:** To strongly connect two ideas. - التأكيد على فكرتين مترابطتين بقوة. **STRUCTURE:** $\longrightarrow$ Not only + auxiliary + subj. + verb, but + subj. + also + V e.g. Normal: - Food waste does not only cost money, but it also harms the environment. Fronting: - Not only does food waste cost money, but it also harms the environment. **ADVANCED POINT:** - إذا جاءت not only داخل الجملة وليست في بدايتها، فلا يحدث تقديم للفعل المساعد. e.g.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Not Only

curriculum_chunks.content: - إذا جاءت not only داخل الجملة وليست في بدايتها، فلا يحدث تقديم للفعل المساعد. e.g. - Food waste not only costs money but also harms nature.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 3. Not Only

curriculum_chunks.content: التقديم باستخدام هذه العبارات **FUNCTION:** To show that one action happened soon after another - التعبير عن حدوث فعل مباشرة بعد فعل آخر **STRUCTURE:** $\longrightarrow$ No sooner + had + subject + p.p. + than $\longrightarrow$ Hardly/Scarcely + had + subject + p.p. + when / before e.g. Normal: - She had no sooner opened the package than she noticed the smell. Fronting: - No sooner had she opened the package than she noticed the smell. **ADVANCED POINT:** $\longrightarrow$ no sooner ...
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4. No sooner / Hardly / Scarcely

curriculum_chunks.content: **ADVANCED POINT:** $\longrightarrow$ no sooner ... + than $\longrightarrow$ hardly/scarcely ... + when/before.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 4. No sooner / Hardly / Scarcely

curriculum_chunks.content: التقديم باستخدام هذه العبارات **FUNCTION:** To emphasize degree or intensity. - تأكيد الدرجة أو الشدة. **STRUCTURE:** $\longrightarrow$ So + adjective/adverb + auxiliary + subj. + V + that $\longrightarrow$ Such + noun phrase + V + subj. + that e.g. Normal: - The problem is so serious that action is needed. Fronting: - So serious is the problem that action is needed. **ADVANCED POINT:** This structure is formal and powerful, so it should not be overused.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5. So / Such fronting

curriculum_chunks.content: **ADVANCED POINT:** This structure is formal and powerful, so it should not be overused. - إذا هذا التركيب رسمي وقوي التأثير؛ لذلك لا ينبغي الإفراط في استخدامه. <!-- بداية الصفحة 180 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: 5. So / Such fronting

curriculum_chunks.content:
**تقديم المكمل**

**FUNCTION:** To emphasize an adjective or noun phrase describing the subject.
- إبراز صفة أو وصف مهم للفاعل.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Complement + V + subject

e.g.
Normal: - Education is most important of all.
Fronting: - Most important of all is education.

**ADVANCED POINT:**
- يعمل هذا النوع أفضل مع التعبيرات الرسمية، وقد تبدو بعض صوره أدبية.
curriculum_chunks.heading: 6. Complement fronting

**القلب مع / Here / There**

**FUNCTION:** To point to something appearing, existing, or happening.

**STRUCTURE:** $\rightarrow$ Here / There + V + noun subject

e.g.

Fronting: Here comes the delivery truck.

**ADVANCED POINT:**
With pronoun subjects, use normal order.

curriculum_chunks.content: **Introduction** This report looks at the main reasons why food is wasted(1) in Egyptian homes. It uses information from consumer surveys(2) and local studies(3). The results show that food waste in Egypt is a serious(4) problem that needs to be addressed(5). **Findings (Causes):** In Egypt, one common(6) cause of food waste is buying more food than a family can use. During Ramadan, some families may prepare or purchase a large amount of food to welcome guests and express generosity(7).
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Causes of Food Waste in Egyptian Homes (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Although generosity is a positive and valued tradition, poor planning can sometimes lead to more food being prepared than needed. As a result, some of the extra food may be wasted. A second important cause is storing food incorrectly(8). Many homes do not have good refrigerators(9) or dry storage(10). As a result, fresh food — especially bread, fruit, and vegetables — goes bad faster than it should. Bread waste alone is a major issue in Egypt.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Causes of Food Waste in Egyptian Homes (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Bread waste alone is a major issue in Egypt. A third cause is confusion(11) about dates on food packages(12). Many people throw away food on or before its "best before" date. However, 'best before' only means that the taste or quality(13) might change — it does not mean the food is unsafe(14). The 'use by' date is the one that tells you when food is no longer safe(15) to eat. **Recommendations:** Based on these findings(16), this report suggests three actions.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Causes of Food Waste in Egyptian Homes (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: **Recommendations:** Based on these findings(16), this report suggests three actions. First, schools should teach students about food shopping and storage from an early age. Second, shops should be required to give safe leftover(17) food to food banks(18) rather than throw it away. Third, food labels(19) should be made clearer so that people understand the difference between 'best before' and 'use by'. **Conclusion** The evidence(20) shows that most food waste in Egypt can be reduced(21) through education and better habits(22).
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Causes of Food Waste in Egyptian Homes (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: The evidence(20) shows that most food waste in Egypt can be reduced(21) through education and better habits(22). These changes do not cost a lot of money. If these recommendations(23) are followed, the amount of food waste in Egyptian homes could go down significantly(24) within a few years.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Causes of Food Waste in Egyptian Homes (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Every day, by the time most teenagers in Egypt have had breakfast, they have already made more **brand choices**(1) than they realize. The phone that wakes them up is one of the most **recognized**(2) **devices**(3) in the world. The shoes by the door carry a **tick**(4) that is far more famous than the company's actual name. Furthermore, the cereal box on the table **features**(5) a **cartoon**(6) bird that has remained unchanged longer than many brands have survived. None of this is an **accident**(7).
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: None of this is an **accident**(7). The biggest companies **invest**(8) more **heavily**(9) in **brand-building**(10) than in almost anything else. This is because a **well-known**(11) brand is more **valuable**(12) than any single product. In addition, they spend more on emotional **storytelling**(13) than on simply describing what their products do. A brand is much more than a logo. It is a set of feelings and ideas, and the strongest brands build those feelings more carefully and more consistently than smaller companies ever could.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: When brand X puts its tick on a shoe and writes "Just Do It", it is selling not only shoes, but also the idea that the person who wears them is stronger, more **determined**(14), and more ready for a challenge than someone who does not. Similarly, when a phone brand presents a new phone in a clean white room, it is selling the idea that its products are simpler, more **elegant**(15), and more **desirable**(16) than anything else on the **market**(17). **اختيارات العلامات التجارية** (1) التجارية
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: A **branded**$^{(18)}$ product is almost always more **expensive**$^{(19)}$ than a similar **unbranded**$^{(20)}$ one. Even though the quality difference is often smaller than people expect, they still choose the brand because the feeling it gives them feels **worth**$^{(21)}$ far more than the price difference.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (1)

curriculum_chunks.content: Psychologists who study how people make choices have found something interesting. When people see the **logo**$^{(22)}$ of their favorite brand, the part of the brain linked to personal **identity**$^{(23)}$ becomes more **active**$^{(24)}$ than when they see an unknown **label**$^{(25)}$. As a result, choosing a brand is rarely a simple or purely **practical**$^{(26)}$ decision.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: As a result, choosing a brand is rarely a simple or purely **practical**$^{(26)}$ decision. This means that when someone chooses X over Z, they are often making a **deeper choice**$^{(27)}$ than simply picking a more comfortable shoe — they are saying something about who they are, or who they most want to be. Understanding why we prefer one brand to another can be an important step towards **mindful consumption**$^{(28)}$.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: Understanding why we prefer one brand to another can be an important step towards **mindful consumption**$^{(28)}$. For instance, for many young people in Egypt, wearing the most popular brand feels more important than wearing the most practical one, because brands have become one of the most powerful languages we use to show where we **belong**$^{(29)}$. Admittedly, not everyone is equally influenced by brand image.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: Admittedly, not everyone is equally influenced by brand image. Although companies benefit greatly from this power, the influence of brands also raises one of the most important questions in modern life: are we truly free when we make choices, or do companies create our **preference**$^{(30)}$ for us? On the other hand, understanding how brands work gives us a real **advantage**$^{(31)}$ as consumers. This helps us avoid blind brand loyalty, where we buy a product based on emotion rather than quality.
curriculum_chunks.heading: More Than a Logo: How Brands Shape What We Buy (2)

curriculum_chunks.content: The most successful brands do not just sell products. They sell the feeling of **belonging**$^{(32)}$ somewhere. Consequently, this feeling becomes stronger, and far more personal. It also becomes harder to **resist**$^{(33)}$ than any simple **advertisement**$^{(34)}$ could ever be. Overall, the more **aware**$^{(35)}$ we are of how brands shape our thinking, the better and freer our choices can become. **Word List** - (18) ذو علامة تجارية - (19) غالي - (20) بلا علامة تجارية - (21) يستحق - (22) شعار - (23) هوية

curriculum_chunks.content: Many teenagers use **social media**(1) every day without thinking about how these **apps**(2) really work. Although these **platforms**(3) seem free, they actually **collect information**(4) about users' **behavior**(5) and **interests**(6). Apps are carefully **designed**(7) to keep people online longer through **features**(8) that make it hard to stop **scrolling**(9). While social media has **benefits**(10), it is important for users to understand how their time and **attention**(11) are being used.
curriculum_chunks.heading: Digital Consumption

curriculum_chunks.content: **1. You have probably heard this phrase before:** 'If you are not paying for the **product**(12), you are the product.' Most people use social media apps for free. But nothing is ever truly free. Every minute you spend scrolling, the app is collecting **data**(13) about you — what you like, what you **ignore**(14), how long you stop on each image, and what makes you **react**(15). This data is then sold to companies who want to show you **advertisements**(16).
curriculum_chunks.heading: Listening Text

curriculum_chunks.content: This data is then sold to companies who want to show you **advertisements**(16). Your time and attention are not free; they are being bought and sold. **2. Apps are designed to keep you online for as long as possible.** Features like **infinite scroll**(17) where the **feed**(18) never ends, and **autoplay**(19), where the next video starts automatically were not created by accident. They were built by teams of **designers**(20) and **professionals**(21) whose job was to make you stay on the app.

curriculum_chunks.content: This paragraph discusses the weaknesses or limitations fairly. The writer should avoid being too harsh and should use a balanced, professional tone. تناقش هذه الفقرة بنصاف نقاط الضعف أو النواقص. ويجب أن يتجنب الكاتب القسوة الزائدة وأن يستخدم أسلوبًا متوازنًا ومهنيًا. **Purpose:** الغرض To show balance by explaining what could be improved or what may cause problems. إظهار التوازن من خلال توضيح ما يمكن تحسينه أو ما قد يسبب مشكلات. **Useful Expressions:** - It is worth noting that ...

curriculum_chunks.content: الخاتمة The conclusion summarises the writer's overall judgement. It states who the writer would recommend the subject to and why. It should end with a memorable final sentence. تلخص الخاتمة الحكم العام للكاتب، وتوضح لمن يوصي بهذا الشيء ولماذا، وينبغي أن تنتهي بجملة أخيرة مؤثرة. **Purpose:** الغرض To give the final judgement and make a clear recommendation. تقديم الحكم النهائي وإعطاء توصية واضحة. **Useful Expressions:** - Overall, I would recommend ... to ... - In conclusion, ... is suitable for ...

curriculum_chunks.content: Sale events(1) make people feel excited and believe they are saving(2) money! However, companies use clever tricks(3) to influence(4) our decisions and push us to buy more. These tricks create urgency(5) and make products seem more valuable(6) than they really are. In the end, many people spend(7) more than they planned, even when they think they are saving. (1) أحدث التخفيضات (2) التوفير (3) خدع (4) يؤثر في (5) إلحاح / استعجال (6) قيّم (7) ينفق (8) مشتريات (9) مسبقًا
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Psychology of the Sale

curriculum_chunks.content: (4) يؤثر في (5) إلحاح / استعجال (6) قيّم (7) ينفق (8) مشتريات (9) مسبقًا (10) اختيارات ذكية (11) يخدع بـ (12) تجنب الخسارة (13) جذاب (14) العقل / الدماغ (15) فرصة (16) مخزون (17) عدّ تنازلي (18) إجمالا (19) مصمم
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Psychology of the Sale

curriculum_chunks.content: Every year, millions of people around the world wait for events like Black Friday to go shopping. They feel excited as they plan their purchases(8) in advance(9) and they believe they are making smart choices(10). But are they really saving money, or are they falling for(11) a set of very clever tricks? One of the most common tricks is called loss aversion(12). Imagine a jacket that costs 400 Egyptian pounds. You do not really need it.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Tricks Behind Sale Events

curriculum_chunks.content: Imagine a jacket that costs 400 Egyptian pounds. You do not really need it. Then a sign appears: "Was 800 LE, Now 400 LE, Save 50%!" Suddenly, the jacket feels much more attractive(13). Your brain(14) tells you, 'If I don't buy it, I will lose the chance(15) to save 400 pounds.' Of course, you have not lost anything, but that is how our brains work. Not buying something feels like a loss. Sale events also use other tricks.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Tricks Behind Sale Events

curriculum_chunks.content: Not buying something feels like a loss. Sale events also use other tricks. Phrases like 'Only 3 left in stock(16)!' create a feeling of urgency. You feel that you must decide immediately or you will miss the chance. When you see many other people buying something, you think it must be a good idea. And countdown(17) clocks on websites force you to decide quickly, before you have time to think carefully. All three tricks work together to push you towards buying.
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Tricks Behind Sale Events

curriculum_chunks.content: All three tricks work together to push you towards buying. Research has found something surprising: people who shop during sales actually spend more money overall(18) than people who do not. They feel they have saved money, but in fact they have spent more. The sale is not designed(19) to save you money. It is designed to make you spend more and feel happy about it. <!-- بداية الصفحة 224 -->
curriculum_chunks.heading: The Tricks Behind Sale Events
